+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the

The bouquet theorem \Cref{thm:bouquet-two-branch-resolution} then supplies an explicit chosen family of examples, namely open-star good covers of a fixed finite model of $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$, for which the acyclic-cover hypothesis is automatic and the pure two-branch resolution kernels can be classified explicitly: a finite abelian group $G$ occurs precisely when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group. +\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[

+ d(G)\leq 2\beta

+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology

+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary

+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an

-The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. +We now describe the framework.  An information state
+$p=(\Gamma_p,R_p)$ is a nonempty team $R_p$ of assignments with common finite
+context $\Gamma_p$.  We write $M,p\Vdash\varphi$ when every assignment in
+$R_p$ satisfies $\varphi$ in the ordinary Tarskian sense.  Thus $\Vdash$ is

+Kripke--Joyal forcing.  Refinement enlarges the context and may restrict the

+truth-preserving reduct expansions, rather than conservative extensions,

-The second part begins once the set-valued local-object functor is enriched by groupoid-valued data. \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity} gives a rigidity statement for representative-rigid lifts: if the local-object presheaf is slice-separated and a realization prestack admits a strict functorial choice of representatives and is globally conservative at the terminal fibre, then the sheafification unit is surjective there; under $H^1$-vanishing and the same slice-separatedness, this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf at the terminal fibre. Thus gluing-level nullity is necessarily tied to genuinely gluing-sensitive lift data. \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} identifies the canonicity that survives at this level: once the sheafified local object functor has been lifted to a banded realization stack, the branch obstruction map to derived $H^2$ is intrinsic up to equivalence of banded extensions. +\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and
+$K_1+K_2=G$ if and only if
+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
+arbitrary empirical model.
 
-Our starting point is the extension chain
+The standard input is as follows.  We use universal satisfaction on nonempty
+teams of assignments, presheaves and their sheafifications, stackification of
+categories fibred in groupoids, the classification of banded gerbes by
+Giraud's $H^2$, the \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison on the specified Leray
+covers, the universal coefficient theorem, and elementary structure theory
+and duality for finite abelian groups
+\cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}.  Our contributions are the organization
+of these inputs into the stated semantic framework; the comparison between
+matching families and component gerbes under explicit lift hypotheses; the
+presentation-comparison groupoid and the two aggregate quotients; the
+component-forgetting exact sequence; the construction of prescribed
+componentwise homological images; and the preceding finite-group
+classification.
+
+The relation with the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction must be stated
+at the outset.  Their obstruction is a relative \v{C}ech class
 \[
-\mathbb{L}_0 \xhookrightarrow{\iota} \mathbb{L}_1 \preceq \mathbb{L}_2 \preceq \mathbb{L}_3 \preceq \mathbb{L}_4,
+ \gamma_e(s)\in
+ \check H^1(\mathcal M,\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0})
 \]
-where $\mathbb{L}_0$ is the pointwise layer, $\mathbb{L}_1$ is the information-state forcing layer, $\mathbb{L}_2$ adds local objects and site structure, $\mathbb{L}_3$ adds branchwise obstruction data, and $\mathbb{L}_4$ adds refinement dynamics. The map $\mathbb{L}_0\hookrightarrow\mathbb{L}_1$ is a singleton semantic embedding, whereas the later steps are conservative extensions in the sense of \Cref{def:conservative-extension}. Thus the geometric and homological material introduced later does not alter the forcing behaviour of formulas already present in the lower layers.
-The semantics is thus related both to team and imperfect-information semantics \cite{Hodges1997,Vaananen2007,AbramskyPuljujarviVaananen2025} and to the forcing and sheaf-theoretic tradition stemming from Beth, Kripke, Fitting, and Tierney and later developed in topos-theoretic form \cite{Beth1956,Kripke1965,Fitting1969,Tierney1972,Goldblatt2006,Johnstone2002}.
+of a presheaf, equivalently a torsor class indexed by a chosen local section
+\cite{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,Caru2017}.  Our obstruction is the
+derived Giraud class
+\[
+ \omega_v=[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)
+\]
+of a gerbe banded by a sheaf, indexed by a global component section.  These
+classes do not correspond.  What is functorial is only the support-level
+comparison: every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model gives a
+canonical split stack whose component gerbes are neutral.  In particular, a
+strongly contextual model has no global component section from which our map
+could produce its local-section-indexed AMB classes.  Consequently the
+condition $d(G)\leq2\beta$ with $G$ not a cyclic $p$-group does not transfer to
+bare empirical models; a band and a non-split banded stack lift would have to
+be supplied as additional data.  This is proved precisely in
+\Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface,thm:unique-branch-contextuality-comparison}.
 
-The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. We then prove in \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} that the predicates $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, and $\Null^{\mathrm{glue}}_s$ are not definable by automorphism-invariant, constant-free formulas of the $\mathbb{L}_1$-reduct with one free reference variable. This is only a lower-bound statement for the comparison fragment under consideration, but it isolates a genuine change of behaviour between $\mathbb L_1$ and $\mathbb L_2$.
+We now describe the framework.  An information state
+$p=(\Gamma_p,R_p)$ is a nonempty team $R_p$ of assignments with common finite
+context $\Gamma_p$.  We write $M,p\Vdash\varphi$ when every assignment in
+$R_p$ satisfies $\varphi$ in the ordinary Tarskian sense.  Thus $\Vdash$ is
+universal team satisfaction, not set-theoretic, Kripke, Beth, or
+Kripke--Joyal forcing.  Refinement enlarges the context and may restrict the
+team, which immediately gives persistence.  Point assignments enter through
+the singleton-state embedding.  The later semantic frameworks add typed data
+while preserving the truth of formulas in the reduct; we call these
+truth-preserving reduct expansions, rather than conservative extensions,
+because consequence conservativity is not asserted without an expansion
+theorem for every lower model.
 
-The second part begins once the set-valued local-object functor is enriched by groupoid-valued data. \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity} gives a rigidity statement for representative-rigid lifts: if the local-object presheaf is slice-separated and a realization prestack admits a strict functorial choice of representatives and is globally conservative at the terminal fibre, then the sheafification unit is surjective there; under $H^1$-vanishing and the same slice-separatedness, this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf at the terminal fibre. Thus gluing-level nullity is necessarily tied to genuinely gluing-sensitive lift data. \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} identifies the canonicity that survives at this level: once the sheafified local object functor has been lifted to a banded realization stack, the branch obstruction map to derived $H^2$ is intrinsic up to equivalence of banded extensions. For such an extension, visible value classes are the global sections of the sheaf of connected components (\Cref{thm:visible-value-components}), each visible branch determines a banded component gerbe (\Cref{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}), and, on slice-separated reference slices, \Cref{thm:gerbe-null-semantics} identifies gluing-level absence with the existence of visible branches together with non-neutrality of the corresponding component gerbes.
+For an admissible parameter $r$ at $p$, the paper specifies a thin
+reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$, its base object
+$a=[r]_p$, and a presheaf of local sections
+$F_{p,s}:\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.  A matching family
+without an element of $F_{p,s}(a)$ is the set-valued failure studied here.
+The forward implication from a matching family to a section of the
+sheafification is formal; the converse holds when
+$F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_{p,s}/a}$ is separated
+(\Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification,thm:sheafification-characterization}).
+The predicates expressing a matching family, a global section, and matching
+without amalgamation are not definable in the automorphism-invariant,
+constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct
+(\Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility}).
 
-The empirical-model interface gives a sharp limit to this canonicity.  \Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface} proves that every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical split realization-stack extension, pseudonatural under ordinary refinements of measurement contexts, but every component gerbe in that extension is neutral.  The Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa class is a relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ class of a presheaf, equivalently a torsor class \cite{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,Caru2017}; it is indexed by a chosen local section.  By contrast, the Giraud map here is a derived $H^2$ class for a sheaf band, indexed by a global component, and for a strongly contextual model that indexing set is empty.  Thus the canonical split construction supplies no non-split banded data, and no branch map of the present kind can recover the AMB classes on all finite empirical models without an additional degree-shifting construction. Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-ghz} exhibits only a chosen split GHZ/Mermin lift.
+Gerbe-valued obstructions require extra, noncanonical structure.  A
+gluing-sensitive banded lift datum consists of a banded groupoid lift of $F$,
+its stackification together with an identification of its component sheaf
+with $aF$, essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre, and a
+\v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypothesis.  A section
+$v\in\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)\cong(aF)(a)$ determines a full component gerbe
+$\mathfrak G_v$ and hence a Giraud class $\omega_v$.  Under the stated
+separatedness, representability, and comparison hypotheses, matching without
+amalgamation is equivalent to the existence of global component sections with
+all corresponding component gerbes non-neutral
+(\Cref{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition,thm:gerbe-null-semantics}).  A
+strictly pullback-stable representative choice imposes a useful rigidity
+condition: together with terminal-fibre essential surjectivity it forces the
+sheafification unit to be onto at the terminal object
+(\Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity}).

+Fix next a global component section, a finite nerve representative, and a
+constant finite abelian band $A$.  The universal coefficient map evaluates
+the class on second homology,
+\[
+ \operatorname{ev}_{\omega}:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow A.
+\]
+We write $K_\omega=\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ for its
+homological image and $Q_\omega=\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)
+=A/K_\omega$ for its homological cokernel.  These are invariants of an object
+of the presentation-comparison groupoid and transport functorially along the
+chosen comparison zigzags; no path independence is claimed.  A class with
+zero $H_2$ evaluation is precisely a class in the $\operatorname{Ext}^1$
+kernel of the universal coefficient sequence.  This separates the
+homology-evaluation quotient from the more presentation-dependent quotient by
+the subgroup generated by the coordinates of a chosen cocycle.
 
-The homological part of the paper starts only after one visible branch, one finite nerve presentation, and one constant finite abelian band have been fixed. What matters for the semantics, at a fixed presentation, is the presentation-object image

-When several visible branches are present, one obtains branch-sensitive and branch-uniform quotients, related by the short exact sequence of \Cref{thm:branch-comparison-exact-sequence}. -Under the same fixed finite-nerve, constant-band, $H_1=0$, and mixed-realization hypotheses, if $H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z^\beta$, \Cref{cor:torsion-free-h2-classification} shows that the realizable hidden subgroups are exactly the subgroups of $A$ generated by at most $\beta$ elements. +\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

  294: \begin{lemma}[Slice-separated descent of refined equality]\label{lem:slice-separated-refined-equality}
  295: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site with pullbacks of covering families, let $F$
  296: be a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$, and let $X$ be an object. Suppose
  297: that $F$ is separated at every object of the slice $\mathcal C/X$. If
  298: \[
  299: \{X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}
  300: \]

  302: refined-overlap condition: for every pair $(i,j)$, writing
  303: $X_{ij}:=X_i\times_X X_j$, the two restrictions of $\sigma_i$ and
  304: $\sigma_j$ to $X_{ij}$ become equal after some covering family of
  305: $X_{ij}$, then the family $(\sigma_i)_i$ is a strict matching family:
  306: \[
  307: \res_{X_{ij}}^{X_i}(\sigma_i)=\res_{X_{ij}}^{X_j}(\sigma_j)

  309: \]

  311: 
  312: \begin{proof}

  314: $\mathcal C/X$. By hypothesis $F$ is separated at $X_{ij}$. The two
  315: sections
  316: \[

  318: \qquad
  319: \res_{X_{ij}}^{X_j}(\sigma_j)
  320: \]
  321: agree after a cover of $X_{ij}$, so separatedness at $X_{ij}$ forces
  322: their equality in $F(X_{ij})$. This is exactly the strict matching
  323: condition.
  324: \end{proof}

  326: \begin{lemma}[Equality in the unit is local equality]\label{lem:sheafification-unit-equality-local}
  327: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site with pullbacks of covering families, let
  328: $F$ be a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$, and let
  329: $u:F\to aF$ be the sheafification unit. If
  330: \[
  331: u_X(\sigma)=u_X(\tau)
  332: \qquad
  333: (\sigma,\tau\in F(X)),
  334: \]
  335: then there is a covering family $\{X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ such that
  336: \[
  337: \res_{X_i}^{X}(\sigma)=\res_{X_i}^{X}(\tau)
  338: \qquad(\forall i\in I).
  339: \]
  340: Conversely, equality after such a cover implies
  341: $u_X(\sigma)=u_X(\tau)$.
  342: \end{lemma}
  343: 
  344: \begin{proof}
  345: For the plus construction, the two unit representatives of
  346: $\sigma,\tau\in F(X)$ are represented by the identity cover of $X$. Their
  347: images in $F^+(X)$ are equal exactly when, after a covering refinement of
  348: that identity cover, the restrictions of $\sigma$ and $\tau$ agree in
  349: $F$. Applying the same statement to the unit
  350: $F^+\to(F^+)^+=aF$, equality of $u_X(\sigma)$ and $u_X(\tau)$ gives a cover
  351: $\{Y_j\to X\}$ on which the two corresponding sections of $F^+$ agree.
  352: For each $j$, equality in $F^+(Y_j)$ gives a further cover
  353: $\{X_{ji}\to Y_j\}_i$ on which the restrictions of $\sigma$ and $\tau$
  354: agree in $F$. By transitivity, the composites $X_{ji}\to X$ form the
  355: required cover. The converse follows because $aF$ is a sheaf: if the two
  356: unit sections agree after a cover, separatedness of the sheaf $aF$ forces
  357: them to agree over $X$.
  358: \end{proof}

  466: \subsection{Banded groupoid lifts and connected components}
  467: 
  468: The presheaf $F_{p,s}$ records only isomorphism classes of local lift objects. To recover gerbes and cohomology one needs a groupoid-valued lift whose connected components give back $F_{p,s}$ after sheafification. We use the standard prestack, stackification, and banded-gerbe conventions of \cite{Giraud1971,MacLaneMoerdijk1994,Moerdijk2002,StacksProject}. Once an abelian band has been fixed, split lifts always exist; the substantive issue is whether a chosen lift is gluing-sensitive at the terminal fibre.
  469: 
  470: \begin{definition}[Banded groupoid lift and stackification]\label{def:realization-prestack}
  471: Fix an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, and write
  472: \[
  473: a=[r]_p,
  474: \qquad
  475: \mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a.
  476: \]
  477: A \emph{banded groupoid lift} for $r$ at $p$ over the pullback-based slice site is a category fibred in groupoids
  478: \[
  479: \mathfrak P_r\to \mathcal C_a
  480: \]
  481: such that:
  482: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
  483: \item the pre-stackification connected-component presheaf is the restriction of the presheaf of local sections,
  484: \[
  485: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\cong F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a};
  486: \]
  487: \item for every object $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$ and every $x\in \mathfrak P_r(U)$, the automorphism sheaf
  488: \[
  489: \underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(x)
  490: \]
  491: on $\mathcal C_a/U$ is functorially identified with the restriction of a fixed abelian sheaf $\Band$ on $\mathcal C_a$.
  492: \end{enumerate}
  493: Write
  494: \[
  495: \mathfrak L_r:=a(\mathfrak P_r)
  496: \]
  497: for the stackification of $\mathfrak P_r$ in groupoids \cite[Tag 02ZP]{StacksProject}.
  498: \end{definition}
  499: 
  500: \begin{proposition}[Separated split banded groupoid lift]\label{prop:split-realization-prestack}
  501: Let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ be admitted at $p$, write
  502: \[
  503: a=[r]_p,\qquad \mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a,
  504: \]
  505: and let $\Band$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal C_a$. There is a canonical split banded groupoid lift
  506: \[
  507: \mathfrak P_r^{\mathrm{spl}}\to\mathcal C_a
  508: \]
  509: with band $\Band$ and connected-component presheaf
  510: \[
  511: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r^{\mathrm{spl}})
  512: \cong F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}.
  513: \]
  514: Explicitly, for every object $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$, the groupoid
  515: $\mathfrak P_r^{\mathrm{spl}}(U)$ has object set $F_{p,s}(U)$ and
  516: \[
  517: \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak P_r^{\mathrm{spl}}(U)}(\sigma,\tau)=
  518: \begin{cases}
  519: \Band(U),& \sigma=\tau,\\
  520: \varnothing,& \sigma\ne\tau,
  521: \end{cases}
  522: \]
  523: with composition given by addition in $\Band(U)$. For a morphism
  524: $f:V\to U$ in $\mathcal C_a$, restriction sends $\sigma$ to
  525: $\res_V^U(\sigma)$ and sends an automorphism $b\in\Band(U)$ to its
  526: restriction $b|_V\in\Band(V)$.
  527: 
  528: This split prestack is separated as a prestack in groupoids, in the
  529: sense that every isomorphism presheaf is a sheaf, if and only if the
  530: restricted presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$ is
  531: slice-separated in the sense of \Cref{def:slice-separated-local-object}.
  532: \end{proposition}
  533: 
  534: \begin{proof}
  535: The displayed rule defines a contravariant pseudofunctor from
  536: $\mathcal C_a$ to groupoids. Since $\mathcal C_a$ is thin, there are no
  537: nontrivial coherence choices to make: functoriality of the object maps is
  538: the functoriality of $F_{p,s}$, and functoriality on automorphisms is the
  539: restriction functoriality of the sheaf $\Band$. The associated category
  540: over $\mathcal C_a$ is therefore fibred in groupoids. Its connected
  541: components over $U$ are exactly the objects $F_{p,s}(U)$, because
  542: distinct objects have no morphisms between them and each automorphism
  543: group is connected to its own object only. Hence
  544: \[
  545: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r^{\mathrm{spl}})(U)\cong F_{p,s}(U)
  546: \]
  547: naturally in $U$.
  548: 
  549: For an object $\sigma\in F_{p,s}(U)$, the automorphism presheaf on
  550: $\mathcal C_a/U$ is
  551: \[
  552: V\longmapsto \operatorname{Aut}(\sigma|_V)=\Band(V),
  553: \]
  554: so its sheafification is already the restriction $\Band|_{\mathcal C_a/U}$.
  555: Thus $\mathfrak P_r^{\mathrm{spl}}$ is a banded groupoid lift with band
  556: $\Band$.
  557: 
  558: It remains to prove the separatedness criterion. Suppose first that
  559: $F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$ is separated on the slice. Let $\sigma,\tau\in
  560: F_{p,s}(U)$ and let $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ be a cover. A matching
  561: family of local isomorphisms
  562: \[
  563: \alpha_i:\sigma|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau|_{U_i}
  564: \]
  565: can exist only when
  566: \[
  567: \sigma|_{U_i}=\tau|_{U_i}
  568: \qquad(\forall i).
  569: \]
  570: Separatedness on the slice then gives $\sigma=\tau$. The local isomorphisms
  571: $\alpha_i$ are therefore sections of the sheaf $\Band$ over the $U_i$,
  572: and their matching condition is exactly the sheaf matching condition for
  573: $\Band$. Since $\Band$ is a sheaf, the $\alpha_i$ glue uniquely to a
  574: global element of $\Band(U)$, hence to a unique global isomorphism
  575: $\sigma\to\tau$. Thus every isomorphism presheaf is a sheaf.
  576: 
  577: Conversely, assume that $\mathfrak P_r^{\mathrm{spl}}$ is separated. Let
  578: $\sigma,\tau\in F_{p,s}(U)$ have equal restrictions on a cover
  579: $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$. The identity element of $\Band(U_i)$ gives an
  580: isomorphism
  581: \[
  582: \sigma|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau|_{U_i}
  583: \]
  584: for every $i$, and these identities form a matching family. Separatedness
  585: of the isomorphism presheaf glues them to a global isomorphism
  586: $\sigma\to\tau$ in the split groupoid. Such a global isomorphism exists
  587: only when $\sigma=\tau$. Therefore $F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$ is separated
  588: at every $U$, which is separatedness on the slice.
  589: \end{proof}
  590: 
  591: \begin{proposition}[Consequences of a chosen gluing-sensitive banded lift datum]\label{thm:gluing-sensitive-realization}
  592: Let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ be admitted at a state $p$, and suppose $r$ is equipped with a gluing-sensitive banded lift datum in the sense of \Cref{def:gluing-sensitive-realization}. Then the later branch-obstruction theory depends on this extra datum, rather than on the split prestack of \Cref{prop:split-realization-prestack}, as follows:
  593: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
  594: \item the sheafified global sections of $r$ are identified with $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$ via \Cref{thm:visible-value-components};
  595: \item if the cofinal gerbe-adapted-cover hypothesis of \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction} is added, then each global component section determines a component gerbe as in \Cref{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition};
  596: \item if, in addition, the terminal-fibre essential surjectivity above is used as essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre over $a$, and the slice site associated to the parameter is separated on the slice when the strict predicate \(\CompSec_s\) is invoked, then the comparison between global sections and neutral component gerbes is exactly the one proved later in \Cref{prop:global-sections-vs-neutral-components} and \Cref{thm:gerbe-null-semantics}.
  597: \end{enumerate}
  598: \end{proposition}
  599: 
  600: \begin{proof}
  601: Clause \textup{(ii)} of \Cref{def:gluing-sensitive-realization} identifies the connected components of the chosen stack $\mathfrak L_r$ with the sheafification of the presheaf of local sections. Combined with \Cref{def:realization-prestack}(ii), this is the stack-theoretic input used later to define global component sections and their component gerbes. Global conservativity at $a$ supplies the comparison between stack-global sections and actual global lift objects via \Cref{prop:no-new-global-objects}. Finally, the acyclic cover data in \Cref{def:gluing-sensitive-realization} are exactly the hypotheses invoked in \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction}. Together these assumptions are precisely what is needed for the later gerbe and obstruction arguments.
  602: \end{proof}

  604: \begin{proposition}[Components of the stackification]\label{prop:stackification-components}
  605: In the setting of \Cref{def:realization-prestack} over the pullback-based slice site $\mathcal C_a$, so without assuming an ambient meet-semilattice presentation, the sheaf of connected components of $\mathfrak L_r$ is canonically identified with the sheafification of the restricted presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$.
  606: \end{proposition}
  607: 
  608: \begin{proof}
  609: By stackification, the morphism presheaves of $\mathfrak P_r$ are sheafified and every object of $\mathfrak L_r$ is locally in the essential image of $\mathfrak P_r\to \mathfrak L_r$ \cite[Tag 02ZP]{StacksProject}. Passing to isomorphism classes therefore shows that $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)$ is the sheafification of $\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)$. Since stacks in setoids are precisely sheaves of sets \cite[Tag 042Y]{StacksProject}, we obtain
  610: \[
  611: \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)\cong a\bigl(\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\bigr).
  612: \]
  613: Using \Cref{def:realization-prestack}(i), this becomes
  614: \[
  615: \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)\cong a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}.
  616: \qedhere
  617: \]
  618: \end{proof}
  619: 
  620: \begin{proposition}[Naturality of the stackification component map]\label{prop:stackification-component-unit-naturality}
  621: In the setting of \Cref{def:realization-prestack}, the map of component
  622: sheaves induced by the stackification morphism
  623: \[
  624: \iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to a(\mathfrak P_r)=\mathfrak L_r
  625: \]
  626: is, under the identification
  627: \[
  628: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\cong F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}
  629: \quad\text{and}\quad
  630: \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)\cong a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a},
  631: \]
  632: exactly the sheafification unit
  633: \[
  634: u:F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\longrightarrow
  635: a_{p,s}F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}.
  636: \]
  637: Equivalently, for every object \(U\) of the slice and every
  638: \(y\in\mathfrak P_r(U)\),
  639: \[
  640: [\iota_r(y)]=u_U([y])
  641: \]
  642: in \(\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(U)\).
  643: \end{proposition}
  644: 
  645: \begin{proof}
  646: \Cref{prop:stackification-components} identifies
  647: \(\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)\) with the sheafification of
  648: \(\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\). This identification is induced by
  649: the universal morphism from a presheaf to its sheafification: applying
  650: \(\pi_0\) to \(\iota_r\) sends a prestack object to the same local
  651: component, now viewed in the sheaf of components. After the defining
  652: identification
  653: \(\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\cong F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\), this
  654: universal morphism is precisely \(u\).
  655: \end{proof}

  657: \begin{definition}[Essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre]\label{def:global-conservativity}
  658: In the setting of \Cref{def:realization-prestack}, now over a pullback-based slice site $\mathcal C_a$, let
  659: \[
  660: \iota_r:\mathfrak P_r\to \mathfrak L_r:=a(\mathfrak P_r)
  661: \]
  662: be the stackification morphism. We say that $\mathfrak P_r$ is \emph{essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$} if every object of the terminal stack fibre $(\mathfrak L_r)_a$ is isomorphic to the image of some object of the terminal prestack fibre $(\mathfrak P_r)_a$; equivalently, the induced functor
  663: \[
  664: (\iota_r)_a:(\mathfrak P_r)_a\to (\mathfrak L_r)_a
  665: \]
  666: is essentially surjective.
  667: \end{definition}
  668: 
  669: \begin{definition}[Global representability of component sections]\label{def:terminal-component-effectivity}
  670: In the setting of \Cref{def:realization-prestack}, the stackification
  671: $\mathfrak L_r$ has \emph{globally represented component sections} if the canonical
  672: map from isomorphism classes of terminal-fibre objects to terminal sections
  673: of the component sheaf,
  674: \[
  675: \pi_0\bigl(\mathfrak L_r(a)\bigr)\longrightarrow \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a),
  676: \]
  677: is surjective. Equivalently, every section of the sheaf of connected
  678: components over $a$ is represented by an actual object of
  679: $\mathfrak L_r(a)$.
  680: \end{definition}

  682: \begin{proposition}[No new global objects at $a$]\label{prop:no-new-global-objects}
  683: Assume essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre over $a$ in the sense of \Cref{def:global-conservativity} for a banded groupoid lift on the pullback-based slice site $\mathcal C_a$. Then
  684: \[
  685: M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)
  686: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  687: \mathfrak L_r(a)\neq\varnothing.
  688: \]
  689: \end{proposition}
  690: 
  691: \begin{proof}
  692: By \Cref{def:existence-levels} and \Cref{def:realization-prestack}(i),
  693: \[
  694: M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)
  695: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  696: F_{p,s}(a)\neq\varnothing
  697: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  698: \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)(a)\neq\varnothing
  699: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  700: (\mathfrak P_r)_a\neq\varnothing.
  701: \]
  702: If $(\mathfrak P_r)_a\neq\varnothing$, choose $y\in (\mathfrak P_r)_a$. Then $\iota_r(y)\in \mathfrak L_r(a)$, so $\mathfrak L_r(a)\neq\varnothing$. Conversely, if $x\in \mathfrak L_r(a)$, essential surjectivity of $(\iota_r)_a$ yields $y\in (\mathfrak P_r)_a$ with $\iota_r(y)\cong x$, so $(\mathfrak P_r)_a\neq\varnothing$.
  703: \end{proof}

  705: \begin{definition}[Representative-rigid lift]\label{def:representative-rigid-lift}
  706: In the setting of \Cref{def:realization-prestack} over the pullback-based slice site $\mathcal C_a$, a banded groupoid lift
  707: \[
  708: \mathfrak P_r\to \mathcal C_a
  709: \]
  710: is called \emph{representative-rigid} if for every object $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$ there is a map
  711: \[

  713: \]

  717: \[

  719: \]
  720: is $\sigma$;
  721: \item for every morphism $f:V\to U$ in $\mathcal C_a$ and every $\sigma\in F_{p,s}(U)$,
  722: \[
  723: f^*s_U(\sigma)=s_V(\res_V^U(\sigma)).
  724: \]
  725: \end{enumerate}
  726: Here \(f^*\) is computed with respect to a fixed split cleavage of the
  727: fibred groupoid \(\mathfrak P_r\), so pullbacks compose on the nose. Thus
  728: the isomorphism classes of local objects admit a strict functorial choice of

    1: \section{Local objects and matching without amalgamation}\label{sec:null-decomposition}
    2: 
    3: We study the local-object problem attached to an admissible parameter, extending the meet-semilattice formulation of the companion paper \cite{MaZhang2026ConditionalGluingFailure} to the pullback-based sites used here. The basic distinction is between local nonemptiness, existence of a matching family, and existence of a global section.
    4: 
    5: The following standing hypothesis will be used throughout the section and cited explicitly when needed.
    6: 
    7: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(RC)},nosep,leftmargin=3em]
    8: \item\label{hyp:refinement-conservation} \emph{Refinement conservation.} If $q\le p$, then admissible parameters, covers, and compatible local families at $q$ restrict functorially to those at $p$, and a sheafified global section already uniquely determined at $p$ is not split by further refinement.
    9: \end{enumerate}
   10: 
   11: \begin{remark}[Relation to the companion paper]
   12: The companion paper \cite{MaZhang2026ConditionalGluingFailure} develops the same local-object and visible-value framework on meet-semilattice sites. In this section those constructions are recast on the pullback-based sites of \Cref{def:local-reference-frame}, so the sheafification criterion, split banded groupoid lifts, stackification comparison, terminal-fibre conservativity, and sheafified global sections are all stated without assuming that overlaps arise from semilattice meets.
   13: \end{remark}

   15: \subsection{References and local objects}
   16: 
   17: Fix a family of referenceable sorts
   18: \[
   19: S_{\mathrm{ref}}\subseteq S.
   20: \]
   21: For each $s\in S_{\mathrm{ref}}$, the language contains a reference sort $\mathsf{Ref}_s$ and an admissibility predicate $\Adm_s(\cdot)$.
   22: Layer placement is fixed as follows. The sort \(\mathsf{Ref}_s\) and its
   23: equality belong to \(\Sigma_1\); the admissibility predicate
   24: \(\Adm_s\), together with \(\LocSec_s,\CompSec_s,\Sec_s\) and the
   25: site-structure symbols, belongs to \(\Sigma_2\setminus\Sigma_1\). Thus a
   26: lower-fragment formula may quantify over references but cannot define or
   27: mention admission unless the statement explicitly restricts attention to the
   28: admitted subdomain.
   29: 
   30: \begin{definition}[Base objects]\label{def:reference-classes}
   31: For each state $p$ and each referenceable sort $s$, fix a set
   32: \[
   33: \mathcal R_s(p)
   34: \]
   35: and a surjective assignment
   36: \[
   37: r\longmapsto [r]_p\in \mathcal R_s(p)
   38: \]
   39: defined for the admissible parameters $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at $p$. The element $[r]_p$ is called the \emph{base object} of $r$ at $p$. The later reference-refinement site is built on these classes; no further quotient structure is needed here.
   40: \end{definition}
   41: 
   42: \begin{definition}[Reference-refinement site]\label{def:local-reference-frame}
   43: For a state $p$ and a referenceable sort $s$, a \emph{reference-refinement site} consists of the following data.
   44: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
   45: \item A reflexive, transitive refinement relation $\sqsubseteq_{p,s}$ on $\mathcal R_s(p)$.
   46: \item The associated small thin category $\mathcal B_{p,s}$ whose objects are the elements of $\mathcal R_s(p)$ and in which there is a unique morphism
   47: \[
   48: b\longrightarrow a
   49: \]
   50: if and only if $b\sqsubseteq_{p,s} a$.
   51: \item A Grothendieck pretopology $\Cov_{p,s}$ on $\mathcal B_{p,s}$ satisfying the identity, pullback-stability, and transitivity axioms.
   52: \item The standing pullback hypothesis that, for every covering family
   53: \[
   54: \{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I}\in \Cov_{p,s}(a)
   55: \]
   56: and every pair $(i,j)$, the fibre product
   57: \[
   58: a_i\times_a a_j
   59: \]
   60: exists in $\mathcal B_{p,s}$.
   61: \end{enumerate}
   62: The fibre product clause is a condition on the site, not on a later
   63: \v{C}ech cochain display: if two members of a covering family are
   64: disjoint in a concrete presentation, their pullback must still be
   65: represented by an object of the site, typically a strict initial object.
   66: One may omit such empty pullback objects from a nonzero \v{C}ech nerve or
   67: from a cochain complex whose coefficient sheaf has only the zero section
   68: there, but not from the reference-refinement site itself. Because
   69: $\mathcal B_{p,s}$ is thin, the fibre product $a_i\times_a a_j$ is the
   70: meet of $a_i$ and $a_j$ over $a$ whenever that meet exists. We write
   71: \[
   72: \mathcal C_{p,s}:=(\mathcal B_{p,s},\Cov_{p,s})
   73: \]
   74: for the resulting site.
   75: \end{definition}
   76: 
   77: \begin{definition}[Presheaf of local sections]\label{def:local-object-functor}
   78: A \emph{presheaf of local sections} on $(p,s)$ is a contravariant functor
   79: \[
   80: F_{p,s}:\mathcal{B}_{p,s}^{op}\to\mathsf{Set}.
   81: \]
   82: If $b\sqsubseteq_{p,s} a$, the induced restriction map is denoted by
   83: \[
   84: \res_b^a:F_{p,s}(a)\to F_{p,s}(b).
   85: \]
   86: \end{definition}
   87: 
   88: \begin{definition}[Three existence levels]\label{def:existence-levels}
   89: Let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ and assume $M,p\Vdash \Adm_s(r)$. Write $a=[r]_p$.
   90: In the pullback-based reference-refinement site of \Cref{def:local-reference-frame}, overlaps are checked on the fibre products $a_i\times_a a_j$ supplied there, rather than on semilattice meets.
   91: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
   92: \item $M,p\Vdash \LocSec_s(r)$ if some cover $\mathcal U=\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I}\in\Cov_{p,s}(a)$ has $F_{p,s}(a_i)\neq\varnothing$ for every $i\in I$.
   93: \item $M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r)$ if some cover $\mathcal U=\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I}\in\Cov_{p,s}(a)$ carries a matching family $(\sigma_i)_{i\in I}$ with each $\sigma_i\in F_{p,s}(a_i)$ and
   94: \[
   95: \res_{a_i\times_a a_j}^{a_i}(\sigma_i)=\res_{a_i\times_a a_j}^{a_j}(\sigma_j).
   96: \]
   97: \item $M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)$ if the fibre $F_{p,s}(a)$ is nonempty.
   98: \end{enumerate}
   99: \end{definition}
  100: 
  101: \begin{proposition}[Global sections yield compatible local sections]\label{prop:global-implies-compatible-local}
  102: In the pullback-based site of \Cref{def:local-reference-frame}, so without assuming a meet-semilattice presentation of overlaps, if $M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)$, then
  103: \[
  104: M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r)
  105: \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  106: M,p\Vdash \LocSec_s(r).
  107: \]
  108: \end{proposition}
  109: 
  110: \begin{proof}
  111: Let $a=[r]_p$ and choose $\sigma\in F_{p,s}(a)$. The identity axiom for the pretopology gives the trivial cover $\{a\to a\}$. The singleton family $(\sigma)$ is therefore a compatible local family, so both existence of a matching family and local nonemptiness follow immediately.
  112: \end{proof}

  114: \subsection{Sheafification and matching without amalgamation}
  115: 
  116: For fixed $(p,s)$, the reference-refinement site of \Cref{def:local-reference-frame} determines a presheaf
  117: \[
  118: F_{p,s}\in\mathbf{PSh}(\mathcal{B}_{p,s}).
  119: \]
  120: Write

  126: \begin{definition}[Separatedness at an object]\label{def:separated-at-a}
  127: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, let $F$ be a presheaf on $\mathcal C$, and let $a$ be an object of $\mathcal C$. We say that $F$ is \emph{separated at $a$} if for every covering family
  128: \[
  129: \{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
  130: \]
  131: and every pair of sections $\sigma,\tau\in F(a)$, the equalities
  132: \[
  133: \res_{a_i}^{a}(\sigma)=\res_{a_i}^{a}(\tau)
  134: \qquad
  135: (\forall i\in I)
  136: \]
  137: imply $\sigma=\tau$.
  138: \end{definition}
  139: 
  140: \begin{definition}[Separatedness on the slice site associated to the parameter]\label{def:slice-separated-local-object}
  141: For an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at $p$, write
  142: \[
  143: a=[r]_p,
  144: \qquad
  145: \mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a.
  146: \]
  147: The restricted presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$ is \emph{slice-separated} if it is separated at every object of $\mathcal C_a$.
  148: Equivalently, separatedness is required not only at the terminal object
  149: $a$, but also at every cover member, every pullback overlap, and every
  150: object introduced by a refinement inside the slice. This distinction is
  151: used essentially below: equality in a sheafification value over a cover
  152: member gives equality of the original presheaf sections only after a
  153: further cover of that cover member, and the upgrade back to equality over
  154: the cover member itself requires separatedness at that object.
  155: \end{definition}
