+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and
+$K_1+K_2=G$ if and only if
+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
+arbitrary empirical model.

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. -The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. +\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

    1: \section{Component gerbes and component obstruction classes}\label{sec:gerbe-obstruction}
    2: 
    3: From this point on the argument proceeds componentwise relative to a chosen
    4: banded groupoid lift. When derived obstruction classes are needed, the
    5: \v{C}ech--derived comparison package below is also imposed. No unconditional
    6: existence theorem for such data is sought here. This section reorganizes the
    7: gerbe-theoretic obstruction package of the companion paper
    8: \cite{MaZhang2026ConditionalGluingFailure} in the intrinsic
    9: realization-stack language used later. The first result of the section
   10: isolates the canonicity that is available once the sheafified local object
   11: functor has been lifted to a banded stack: the component obstruction class is
   12: intrinsic to the resulting banded stack lift, up to equivalence of
   13: extensions. Since a single reference may carry several sheafified global sections,
   14: the relevant obstruction objects are the corresponding component gerbes
   15: rather than a single global gerbe. The cocycle constructions used below are
   16: the standard local-trivialization constructions for gerbes
   17: \cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Sec.~5]{Breen2006}, together with their
   18: bundle-gerbe counterparts \cite{Murray1996,Brylinski1993}, applied
   19: componentwise in the present setting.
   20: 
   21: We begin by fixing the hypotheses used in the section. Individual statements invoke only the subcollection they require.
   22: 
   23: \begin{definition}[\v{C}ech--derived comparison package]\label{def:cech-derived-comparison-package}
   24: For an admissible parameter \(r:\mathsf{Ref}_s\) at \(p\), a band \(\Band\)
   25: on \(\mathcal C_{p,s}/a\), and a global component section \(v\), a
   26: \emph{\v{C}ech--derived comparison package} consists of a filtered cofinal
   27: family
   28: \[
   29: \Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)\subseteq \Cov_{p,s}(a)
   30: \]
   31: such that every cover \(\mathcal U=\{U_i\to a\}\) in the family has a
   32: \v{C}ech nerve in the slice site, trivializes the band on all intersections
   33: used in degrees \(0,1,2\), and satisfies the following comparison condition:
   34: the canonical refinement map
   35: \[
   36: \varinjlim_{\mathcal U\in\Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)}
   37: \check H^2(\mathcal U,\Band)
   38: \longrightarrow
   39: H^2(\mathcal C_{p,s}/a,\Band)
   40: \]
   41: is an isomorphism. One way to verify this condition is the usual Leray
   42: hypothesis: all nonempty finite intersections appearing in the family are
   43: \(\Band\)-acyclic in every positive degree needed for the derived
   44: comparison. The definition itself, however, records the comparison
   45: isomorphism as the required assumption; the later theorems do not silently
   46: infer derived \(H^2\) from a single \v{C}ech cocycle unless this package, or
   47: the explicit finite good-cover Leray theorem of
   48: \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}, is in force.
   49: \end{definition}
   50: 
   51: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},nosep]
   52: \item\label{hyp:admitted-prestack} An admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$ with $a=[r]_p$, equipped with a banded groupoid lift $\mathfrak P_r \to \mathcal C_a$ and band $\Band$ in the sense of \Cref{def:realization-prestack}.
   53: \item\label{hyp:band-identification} The band $\Band$ is identified with a fixed abelian sheaf on the slice site $\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$.
   54: \item\label{hyp:global-conservativity} The banded groupoid lift $\mathfrak P_r$ is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$ in the sense of \Cref{def:global-conservativity}.
   55: \item\label{hyp:cofinal-gerbe-adapted} For every global component section \(v\), a
   56: \v{C}ech--derived comparison package in the sense of
   57: \Cref{def:cech-derived-comparison-package} has been fixed.
   58: \end{enumerate}
   59: 
   60: When a statement compares global component sections with the strict predicate
   61: \(\CompSec_s\), or with \(\NoAmalg_s\) through that predicate,
   62: it separately assumes that \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice.
   63: Without this separatedness assumption global component sections are only
   64: sheafified sections, and no strict compatible family is asserted.
   65: 
   66: \begin{remark}[\v{C}ech versus derived cohomology]\label{rem:cech-vs-derived}
   67: Hypothesis \ref{hyp:cofinal-gerbe-adapted}, equivalently the package of
   68: \Cref{def:cech-derived-comparison-package}, is the precise comparison
   69: assumption governing the passage between \v{C}ech and derived $H^2$. It
   70: requires the comparison isomorphism itself; acyclicity in positive degrees is
   71: one standard sufficient Leray condition, not a hidden extra assumption unless
   72: explicitly invoked. Without the package, the component obstruction class lives in
   73: the filtered colimit
   74: \[
   75: \varinjlim_{\mathcal U\in \Cov_v^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)} \check H^2(\mathcal U,\Band),
   76: \]
   77: and the non-neutrality statement in \Cref{thm:cech-bridge-compatible-realizations} is purely \v{C}ech-theoretic. With \ref{hyp:cofinal-gerbe-adapted}, this colimit is canonically identified with the derived $H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band)$, and the obstruction class $\omega_v$ is an element of derived cohomology. All theorems in this subsection state explicitly whether they use only the \v{C}ech-level data or additionally require the comparison isomorphism.
   78: \end{remark}
   79: 
   80: \begin{remark}[Relation to the companion paper]
   81: The companion paper \cite{MaZhang2026ConditionalGluingFailure} formulates branch obstructions relative to a chosen gluing-sensitive banded lift prestack and its stackification. The present section isolates the three extensions needed later: the promotion of cover-relative \v{C}ech classes to derived classes $\omega_v$ under \textup{(H4)}, the reformulation of the obstruction theory for arbitrary banded stack lifts of the component sheaf of the sheafified presheaf of local sections, and the componentwise neutrality criteria stated directly in terms of component gerbes.
   82: \end{remark}

   84: \begin{definition}[Component gerbes and component obstruction classes]\label{def:compatible-realization-stack}\label{def:cech-gluing-obstruction}
   85: Fix an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, write
   86: \[

  637: \begin{proposition}[Derived branch classes detect neutrality]\label{prop:derived-branch-classification}
  638: Assume \textup{(H1)}--\textup{(H4)}. For every global component section $v$,
  639: \[
  640: \omega_v=0\ \text{in}\ H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band)
  641: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  642: \mathfrak G_v\ \text{is neutral}.
  643: \]
  644: \end{proposition}
  645: 
  646: \begin{proof}
  647: By \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction}, the derived class $\omega_v$ is the image of the refinement-compatible \v{C}ech classes supplied by \Cref{thm:cech-bridge-compatible-realizations}. The comparison isomorphism in \textup{(H4)} identifies this class with the standard Giraud class of the banded gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$. The vanishing of that derived class is equivalent to neutrality by the classification of banded gerbes by $H^2$ \cite[Chap.~IV]{Giraud1971}, \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}.
  648: \end{proof}

  650: \begin{proposition}[Compatible local sections versus global component sections on separated slices]\label{prop:compsecs-vs-visible-branches}
  651: Assume that $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ is admitted at $p$, admits a banded groupoid lift in the sense of \Cref{def:realization-prestack}, and that $F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$ is separated on the slice. Then global component sections detect strict compatible local realizability, without any terminal-fibre essential-surjectivity or derived-comparison hypothesis:
  652: \[
  653: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\neq\varnothing
  654: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  655: M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r).
  656: \]
  657: \end{proposition}
  658: 
  659: \begin{proof}
  660: By \Cref{thm:visible-value-components},
  661: \[
  662: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \bigl(a_{p,s}F_{p,s}\bigr)(a).
  663: \]
  664: The implication from strict existence of a matching family to
  665: nonemptiness of this sheafification is
  666: \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification}. Conversely, a global component section gives
  667: an element of \((a_{p,s}F_{p,s})(a)\) by the same displayed
  668: identification. The slice-separated hypothesis is exactly the additional
  669: condition needed to strictify that sheafified section: applying
  670: \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} to

  672: matching family of \(F_{p,s}\)-sections on that cover. By
  673: \Cref{def:existence-levels}(ii), this is
  674: \[
  675: M,p\Vdash\CompSec_s(r).
  676: \]
  677: \end{proof}

  679: \begin{lemma}[Terminal-fibre nonemptiness and neutrality]\label{lem:terminal-fibre-neutrality}
  680: Let $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$. Then
  681: \[
  682: \mathfrak G_v(a)\neq\varnothing
  683: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  684: \mathfrak G_v\ \text{is neutral}.
  685: \]
  686: \leanverified{paper_gluing_failure_terminal_fibre_neutrality}
  687: \end{lemma}
  688: 
  689: \begin{proof}
  690: By definition of the gerbe notion used in this paper, neutrality means the existence of a global object over $a$. Therefore it is exactly the same as $\mathfrak G_v(a)\neq\varnothing$.
  691: \end{proof}

  693: \begin{proposition}[Global sections versus neutral component gerbes]\label{prop:global-sections-vs-neutral-components}
  694: \leanverified{paper_gluing_failure_global_sections_vs_neutral_components}
  695: Assume that $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ is admitted at $p$, that it admits a banded groupoid lift in the sense of \Cref{def:realization-prestack}, and that this prestack is essentially surjective on the terminal fibre over $a$ in the sense of \Cref{def:global-conservativity}. Then a global lift object exists exactly when some global component section has a global object:
  696: \[
  697: M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)
  698: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  699: \exists v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)\ \text{such that}\ \mathfrak G_v(a)\neq\varnothing.
  700: \]
  701: Equivalently, by \Cref{lem:terminal-fibre-neutrality}, a global lift object exists exactly when at least one global component section gerbe is neutral.
  702: \end{proposition}
  703: 
  704: \begin{proof}
  705: From \Cref{prop:no-new-global-objects}, $M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)$ iff $\mathfrak L_r(a)\neq\varnothing$.
  706: 
  707: If $\mathfrak L_r(a)\neq\varnothing$, choose $x\in \mathfrak L_r(a)$ and let
  708: \[
  709: v=[x]\in \pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)\cong \Vis_{p,s}(r).
  710: \]
  711: Then $x\in \mathfrak G_v(a)$, so $\mathfrak G_v(a)\neq\varnothing$.
  712: 
  713: Conversely, if $\mathfrak G_v(a)\neq\varnothing$ for some global component section $v$, then $\mathfrak G_v(a)\subseteq \mathfrak L_r(a)$, so $\mathfrak L_r(a)\neq\varnothing$.
  714: \end{proof}

  716: \begin{theorem}[Conditional branched gerbe semantics of matching without amalgamation]\label{thm:gerbe-null-semantics}
  717: Assume \textup{(H1)}--\textup{(H3)} for an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at $p$, and assume in addition that \(F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}\) is separated on the slice. Then the gluing-null condition is exactly the existence of at least one global component section and the non-neutrality of every component gerbe:
  718: \[
  719: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r)
  720: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  721: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\neq\varnothing
  722: \ \text{and}\
  723: \mathfrak G_v\ \text{is non-neutral for every }v\in\Vis_{p,s}(r).
  724: \]
  725: If, in addition, \textup{(H4)} holds, then this is equivalently
  726: \[
  727: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r)
  728: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  729: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\neq\varnothing
  730: \ \text{and}\
  731: \omega_v\neq 0\ \text{in }H^2(\mathcal C_a,\Band)
  732: \text{ for every }v\in\Vis_{p,s}(r).
  733: \]
  734: The companion theorem \cite[Theorem~5.20]{MaZhang2026ConditionalGluingFailure} is the meet-semilattice analogue of this pullback-site formulation.
  735: \end{theorem}
  736: 
  737: \begin{proof}
  738: Because $r$ is admitted, the definition of matching without amalgamation gives
  739: \[
  740: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r)
  741: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  742: M,p\Vdash \CompSec_s(r)\ \text{and}\ M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r).
  743: \]
  744: By \Cref{prop:compsecs-vs-visible-branches}, the compatible-local clause is equivalent to
  745: \[
  746: \Vis_{p,s}(r)\neq\varnothing.
  747: \]
  748: By \Cref{prop:global-sections-vs-neutral-components}, using essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre over $a$ from \textup{(H3)}, the global-section clause is equivalent to the existence of a global component section $v$ with
  749: \[
  750: \mathfrak G_v(a)\neq\varnothing.
  751: \]
  752: By \Cref{lem:terminal-fibre-neutrality}, this is equivalent to the existence of a neutral component gerbe. Therefore
  753: \[
  754: M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r)
  755: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  756: \mathfrak G_v\ \text{is non-neutral for every }v\in\Vis_{p,s}(r),
  757: \]
  758: provided the compatible-local clause has supplied at least one global component section. Combining these two equivalences proves the first displayed characterization.
  759: 
  760: Assume now also \textup{(H4)}. For each global component section $v$, \Cref{prop:derived-branch-classification} gives
  761: \[
  762: \omega_v=0
  763: \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  764: \mathfrak G_v\ \text{is neutral}.
  765: \]
  766: Thus non-neutrality of every component gerbe is equivalent to nonvanishing of every derived branch class $\omega_v$, and the second displayed characterization follows.
  767: \end{proof}

    2: \subsection{Quotients and choice of compatible representatives}
    3: 
    4: We now fix one global component section and a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative. The quotient $A/H_\alpha$ records what remains visible at the level of the chosen cocycle; the presentation-relative quotient considered in the next section removes the dependence on the representative within the specified presentation-comparison groupoid.
    5: 
    6: \begin{definition}[Ordered \v{C}ech convention]\label{def:ordered-cech-convention}
    7: For every finite cover
    8: \[
    9: \mathcal U=\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I}
   10: \]
   11: used in a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative, fix a total order on $I$. The
   12: group $\check C^n(\mathcal U,A)$ is indexed by strictly increasing
   13: nondegenerate tuples
   14: \[
   15: i_0<\cdots<i_n
   16: \]
   17: whose overlap $a_{i_0\cdots i_n}$ is nonempty. If a value is written on an
   18: arbitrary ordered tuple, it denotes the alternating extension from the
   19: increasing tuple: permuting pairwise distinct indices multiplies the value
   20: by the sign of the permutation, and a tuple with a repeated index has value
   21: $0$. In degree $2$, the cocycle identity on every ordered nondegenerate
   22: quadruple is
   23: \[
   24: \alpha_{jkl}-\alpha_{ikl}+\alpha_{ijl}-\alpha_{ijk}=0.
   25: \]
   26: Thus reversing the orientation of a nondegenerate triple replaces
   27: $\alpha_{ijk}$ by $-\alpha_{ijk}$.
   28: \end{definition}
   29: 
   30: \begin{definition}[Finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative]\label{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}
   31: Fix an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, and assume:
   32: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
   33: \item the hypotheses of \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction} hold;
   34: \item a global component section
   35: \[
   36: v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)
   37: \]
   38: has been chosen;
   39: \item the associated component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is banded by a finite abelian group $A$,
   40: \item a finite covering family
   41: \[
   42: \mathcal U=\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I},
   43: \qquad
   44: a=[r]_p,
   45: \]
   46: has been chosen together with a \v{C}ech $2$-cocycle
   47: \[
   48: \alpha=(\alpha_{ijk})\in Z^2(\mathcal U,A)
   49: \]
   50: representing the component obstruction class $\omega_v$, written in the ordered
   51: convention of \Cref{def:ordered-cech-convention}.
   52: \end{enumerate}
   53: Define the \emph{coordinate-image subgroup}
   54: \[
   55: H_\alpha:=\langle \alpha_{ijk}\mid i<j<k\text{ and }a_{ijk}\neq\varnothing\rangle\le A,
   56: \]
   57: and the associated \emph{quotient}
   58: \[
   59: A_{\mathrm{vis}}:=A/H_\alpha.
   60: \]
   61: \end{definition}
   62: 
   63: \begin{remark}[Orientation independence of the generated subgroup]\label{rem:strict-subgroup-orientation}
   64: The definition of $H_\alpha$ is independent of whether one generates from
   65: increasing triples or from all oriented nondegenerate triples. Indeed, any
   66: orientation change replaces a generator $\alpha_{ijk}$ by
   67: $-\alpha_{ijk}$, and the subgroup generated by a subset of an abelian group
   68: is unchanged after replacing any generator by its negative. Degenerate
   69: triples contribute $0$ by \Cref{def:ordered-cech-convention}.
   70: \end{remark}
   71: 
   72: \begin{theorem}[Algebraic quotient generated by a chosen obstruction cocycle]\label{thm:initial-visible-quotient}
   73: In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, let
   74: \[
   75: \pi:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}
   76: \]
   77: be the canonical quotient map. Then:
   78: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
   79: \item the pushed-forward cocycle $\pi_*(\alpha)$ is pointwise zero on every nonempty triple overlap;
   80: \item if $\varphi:A\to B$ is any homomorphism into an abelian group $B$ such that $\varphi(\alpha_{ijk})=0$ for every ordered nondegenerate triple overlap, then there exists a unique homomorphism
   81: \[
   82: \bar\varphi:A_{\mathrm{vis}}\to B
   83: \]
   84: with $\varphi=\bar\varphi\circ\pi$.
   85: \end{enumerate}
   86: Hence \(A_{\mathrm{vis}}\) is the elementary quotient of \(A\) by the
   87: subgroup generated by the displayed cocycle values; equivalently, it is the
   88: initial coefficient quotient through which this chosen obstruction
   89: presentation becomes strictly trivial.
   90: \end{theorem}
   91: 
   92: \begin{proof}
   93: By construction and \Cref{rem:strict-subgroup-orientation}, every oriented
   94: cocycle value $\alpha_{ijk}$ lies in the subgroup $H_\alpha$. Therefore
   95: $\pi(\alpha_{ijk})=0$ for every ordered nondegenerate triple overlap, which
   96: proves (i).
   97: 
   98: For (ii), the hypothesis $\varphi(\alpha_{ijk})=0$ on every ordered
   99: nondegenerate triple overlap implies that every generator of $H_\alpha$
  100: lies in $\ker\varphi$. Hence $H_\alpha\subseteq\ker\varphi$. By the
  101: universal property of the quotient by $H_\alpha$, there exists a unique
  102: homomorphism $\bar\varphi:A/H_\alpha\to B$ satisfying
  103: $\varphi=\bar\varphi\circ\pi$.
  104: \end{proof}
  105: 
  106: The strict quotient $A/H_\alpha$ depends on the chosen cocycle representative $\alpha$, not only on the cohomology class $\omega_v$. The next section removes this dependence: the homological evaluation map $\mathrm{ev}_\omega$ is defined from the class itself, and its cokernel $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^\omega$ is canonical within the homology-equivalent comparison class isolated there. The comparison between the two quotients is given by \Cref{cor:strict-to-intrinsic-visible} and \Cref{prop:chain-vs-homological-visibility}.
  107: 
  108: \begin{definition}[Coboundary action and character annihilating the coordinate-image subgroup channels]\label{def:gauge-invariance-character}
  109: In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, the \v{C}ech $1$-cochain group $C^1(\mathcal U,A)$ acts on cocycles by coboundary translation: a cochain
  110: \[
  111: h=(h_{ij})\in C^1(\mathcal U,A)
  112: \]
  113: sends a cocycle $\alpha$ to the cohomologous cocycle
  114: \[
  115: (h\cdot\alpha)_{ijk}:=\alpha_{ijk}+(\delta h)_{ijk}.
  116: \]
  117: A character $\chi\in\widehat A$ is called \emph{presentation-invariant} for the chosen obstruction presentation if it kills the coordinate-image subgroup $H_\alpha$, equivalently if it factors through the quotient
  118: \[
  119: \pi:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}=A/H_\alpha.
  120: \]
  121: In that case the pushed-forward class $\chi_*[\alpha]$ depends only on the quotient and not on the chosen local trivializations.
  122: \end{definition}
  123: 
  124: \begin{theorem}[Character channels and the cocycle-coordinate quotient]\label{thm:character-definability-barrier}
  125: In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, let
  126: \[
  127: \widehat A:=\mathrm{Hom}(A,\mathbb T),
  128: \]
  129: where $\mathbb T\subseteq\mathbb C^\times$ is the unit circle, and define
  130: \[
  131: H_\alpha^\perp:=\{\chi\in\widehat A\mid \chi(h)=1\text{ for every }h\in H_\alpha\}.
  132: \]
  133: Call a character $\chi\in\widehat A$ \emph{globally admissible} for the obstruction presentation if
  134: \[
  135: \chi(\alpha_{ijk})=1
  136: \]
  137: for every nonempty triple overlap of $\mathcal U$. Then:
  138: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
  139: \item a character $\chi\in\widehat A$ is globally admissible if and only if $\chi\in H_\alpha^\perp$;
  140: \item the quotient map $\pi:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}$ induces a natural isomorphism
  141: \[
  142: \widehat{A_{\mathrm{vis}}}\cong H_\alpha^\perp;
  143: \]
  144: \item consequently, every cocycle-trivializing character factors uniquely through $A_{\mathrm{vis}}$, and a character is presentation-invariant for the chosen obstruction presentation if and only if it lies in $H_\alpha^\perp$.
  145: \end{enumerate}
  146: \end{theorem}
  147: 
  148: \begin{proof}
  149: Since $H_\alpha$ is generated by the cocycle values $\alpha_{ijk}$, a character $\chi$ is trivial on $H_\alpha$ if and only if it is trivial on each generator $\alpha_{ijk}$. This proves (i).
  150: 
  151: For (ii), the quotient map $\pi$ induces by precomposition an injective homomorphism
  152: \[
  153: \pi^*:\widehat{A_{\mathrm{vis}}}\hookrightarrow \widehat A.
  154: \]
  155: Its image consists exactly of the characters on $A$ that are trivial on $\ker\pi=H_\alpha$, namely $H_\alpha^\perp$. Thus $\pi^*$ identifies $\widehat{A_{\mathrm{vis}}}$ with $H_\alpha^\perp$.
  156: 
  157: Clause \textup{(iii)} is just \Cref{def:gauge-invariance-character} rewritten using \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)}.
  158: \end{proof}
  159: 
  160: \begin{corollary}[The quotient is exactly the character-quotient]\label{cor:visible-quotient-character-separation}
  161: In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, for elements $x,y\in A$ the following are equivalent:
  162: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
  163: \item $\pi(x)=\pi(y)$ in $A_{\mathrm{vis}}$;
  164: \item $\chi(x)=\chi(y)$ for every cocycle-trivializing character $\chi\in\widehat A$.
  165: \end{enumerate}
  166: Equivalently, $A_{\mathrm{vis}}$ is the quotient of $A$ obtained by identifying exactly those elements that cannot be separated by cocycle-trivializing characters.
  167: \end{corollary}
  168: 
  169: \begin{proof}
  170: Assume first that $\pi(x)=\pi(y)$. By \Cref{thm:character-definability-barrier}(ii), every cocycle-trivializing character $\chi$ factors as
  171: \[
  172: \chi=\bar\chi\circ\pi
  173: \]
  174: for a unique character $\bar\chi\in\widehat{A_{\mathrm{vis}}}$. Hence
  175: \[
  176: \chi(x)=\bar\chi(\pi(x))=\bar\chi(\pi(y))=\chi(y).
  177: \]
  178: 
  179: Conversely, suppose $\pi(x)\neq\pi(y)$. Then
  180: \[
  181: g:=\pi(x)-\pi(y)\neq 0
  182: \]
  183: in the finite abelian group $A_{\mathrm{vis}}$. By the structure theorem for finite abelian groups \cite{DummitFoote2004}, there is an isomorphism
  184: \[
  185: A_{\mathrm{vis}}\cong \mathbb Z/n_1\mathbb Z\oplus\cdots\oplus \mathbb Z/n_t\mathbb Z
  186: \]
  187: under which the image of $g$ has some nonzero coordinate, say the $k$th. The coordinate character
  188: \[
  189: \psi(z_1,\dots,z_t):=\exp(2\pi i z_k/n_k)
  190: \]
  191: therefore satisfies $\psi(g)\neq 1$. By \Cref{thm:character-definability-barrier}(ii), the character
  192: \[
  193: \chi:=\psi\circ\pi
  194: \]
  195: is globally admissible. Since
  196: \[
  197: \chi(x)\chi(y)^{-1}=\psi(\pi(x)-\pi(y))=\psi(g)\neq 1,
  198: \]
  199: we have $\chi(x)\neq\chi(y)$, contradicting (ii). Thus $\pi(x)=\pi(y)$.
  200: \end{proof}
  201: \leanverified{paper_gluing_failure_visible_quotient_character_separation}
  202: 
  203: \begin{definition}[Fibre-separating auxiliary register]\label{def:auxiliary-strictification-code}
  204: In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, an \emph{fibre-separating auxiliary register} consists of a finite set $R$ and an injective map
  205: \[
  206: \iota:A\hookrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}\times R
  207: \]
  208: such that the first projection recovers the canonical quotient:
  209: \[
  210: \mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota=\pi.
  211: \]
  212: Equivalently, the quotient is kept fixed, while the auxiliary register $R$ resolves the quotient-fibre information inside the fibers of $\pi$.
  213: \end{definition}
  214: 
  215: \begin{theorem}[Fibre size of an auxiliary register]\label{thm:minimal-information-cost-of-strictification}
  216: In the setting of \Cref{def:auxiliary-strictification-code}, every fibre-separating auxiliary register satisfies
  217: \[
  218: |R|\ge |H_\alpha|.
  219: \]
  220: Equivalently,
  221: \[
  222: \log_2 |R|\ge \log_2 |H_\alpha|.
  223: \]
  224: Moreover, this lower bound is sharp.
  225: \leanverified{paper_gluing_failure_minimal_information_cost_of_choice of compatible representatives}
  226: \end{theorem}
  227: 
  228: \begin{proof}
  229: Let $\bar a\in A_{\mathrm{vis}}$. The fiber $\pi^{-1}(\bar a)$ is a coset of $\ker\pi=H_\alpha$, hence has cardinality $|H_\alpha|$. Since $\iota$ is injective and $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota=\pi$, the restriction of $\iota$ to $\pi^{-1}(\bar a)$ lands inside the slice $\{\bar a\}\times R$ and remains injective. Therefore
  230: \[
  231: |H_\alpha|=|\pi^{-1}(\bar a)|\le |\{\bar a\}\times R|=|R|.
  232: \]
  233: This proves the lower bound.
  234: 
  235: To see that it is sharp, take $R:=H_\alpha$. Choose a set-theoretic section $s:A_{\mathrm{vis}}\to A$ of $\pi$. For each $x\in A$, the difference
  236: \[
  237: h(x):=x-s(\pi(x))
  238: \]
  239: lies in $H_\alpha$. Define
  240: \[
  241: \iota(x):=(\pi(x),h(x))\in A_{\mathrm{vis}}\times H_\alpha.
  242: \]
  243: Then $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota=\pi$. If $\iota(x)=\iota(y)$, then $\pi(x)=\pi(y)$ and $h(x)=h(y)$, hence
  244: \[
  245: x=s(\pi(x))+h(x)=s(\pi(y))+h(y)=y.
  246: \]
  247: Thus $\iota$ is injective and $|R|=|H_\alpha|$.
  248: \end{proof}
  249: 
  250: \begin{corollary}[Conservative recovery requires minimum auxiliary register size]\label{cor:conservative-recovery-budget}
  251: For a finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative, no conservative enrichment that leaves the quotient unchanged can restore full \(A\)-resolution with fewer than \(\log_2|H_\alpha|\) bits of auxiliary local state. This is the elementary fiber-counting consequence of quotienting by the coordinate-image subgroup \(H_\alpha\).
  252: \end{corollary}
  253: 
  254: \begin{proof}
  255: Any such enrichment induces an fibre-separating auxiliary register in the sense of \Cref{def:auxiliary-strictification-code}. Apply \Cref{thm:minimal-information-cost-of-strictification}.
  256: \end{proof}
  257: \leanverified{paper_conservative_extension_conservative_recovery_budget}
  258: 
  259: \subsection{A worked finite example}
  260: 
  261: \begin{example}[A one-bit hidden obstruction]\label{ex:one-bit-hidden-obstruction}
  262: Assume an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ together with a three-member cover
  263: \[
  264: \mathcal U=\{a_0,a_1,a_2\to a\},
  265: \qquad
  266: a=[r]_p,
  267: \]
  268: and let the band be the additive group
  269: \[
  270: A=\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z.
  271: \]
  272: Suppose the chosen obstruction presentation is represented by a cocycle whose only nonzero value on a nonempty triple overlap is
  273: \[
  274: \alpha_{012}=2\in \mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z.
  275: \]
  276: Then
  277: \[
  278: H_\alpha=\langle 2\rangle=\{0,2\},
  279: \qquad
  280: A_{\mathrm{vis}}=A/H_\alpha\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z.
  281: \]
  282: 
  283: Thus the quotient identifies $0$ with $2$ and identifies $1$ with $3$. By \Cref{thm:initial-visible-quotient}, this is the initial coefficient quotient through which the chosen obstruction presentation becomes trivial.
  284: 
  285: For $m\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, define a character
  286: \[
  287: \chi_m(x):=\exp(2\pi i mx/4).
  288: \]
  289: Then
  290: \[
  291: \chi_m(\alpha_{012})=\chi_m(2)=(-1)^m,
  292: \]
  293: so \Cref{thm:character-definability-barrier} implies that the cocycle-trivializing characters are exactly
  294: \[
  295: \chi_0
  296: \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  297: \chi_2.
  298: \]
  299: Hence the only surviving linear detection is parity: $\chi_2$ distinguishes the two cosets of $H_\alpha$, while the phase-sensitive channels $\chi_1$ and $\chi_3$ do not factor through the quotient. By \Cref{cor:visible-quotient-character-separation}, the quotient is therefore exactly the quotient detected by all cocycle-trivializing characters.
  300: 
  301: Finally, \Cref{thm:minimal-information-cost-of-strictification} yields
  302: \[
  303: |R|\ge |H_\alpha|=2,
  304: \]
  305: so at least one auxiliary bit is required to recover the full $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$-resolution while keeping the quotient fixed. This lower bound is attained by the code
  306: \[
  307: 0\mapsto (\overline{0},0),\qquad
  308: 2\mapsto (\overline{0},1),\qquad
  309: 1\mapsto (\overline{1},0),\qquad
  310: 3\mapsto (\overline{1},1),
  311: \]
  312: where $\overline{0},\overline{1}\in A_{\mathrm{vis}}\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ and the second component is a one-bit register.
  313: \end{example}

 succeeded in 237ms:
    1: \section{Homological visibility and presentation-relative quotients}
    2: \label{sec:homological-visibility}
    3: 
    4: We now fix one global component section together with a finite nerve representative. The quotient attached to a chosen cocycle still depends on that presentation, so in order to isolate the part determined by the cohomology class itself we pass to the homological evaluation map. Throughout the section we work with one fixed finite cover and the comparison maps coming from the identification of \v{C}ech cochains with simplicial cochains on its finite nerve. The resulting homological image subgroup and quotient are presentation-relative invariants only relative to the homology-equivalent changes of presentation singled out below.
    5: 
    6: We also assume that the chosen cover $\mathcal U$ trivializes the band, so that the coefficients may be viewed as a constant finite abelian group $A$ on the nerve. The case of nontrivial monodromy, which would require local coefficients, is not considered here.
    7: 
    8: \subsection{Finite nerve representatives}
    9: 
   10: \begin{definition}[Finite nerve representative of the obstruction class]\label{def:finite-nerve-presentation}
   11: Fix an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, and assume conditions \textup{(i)}--\textup{(iv)} of \Cref{def:finite-obstruction-presentation}, with the ordered \v{C}ech convention of \Cref{def:ordered-cech-convention}. A \emph{finite nerve representative} of the component obstruction class consists of:
   12: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
   13: \item a finite covering family
   14: \[
   15: \mathcal U=\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I},
   16: \qquad
   17: a=[r]_p,
   18: \]
   19: whose \v{C}ech nerve $N(\mathcal U)$ is finite;
   20: \item a trivialization of the band on $\mathcal U$, so that the band may be viewed as a constant coefficient finite abelian group $A$ on $N(\mathcal U)$;
   21: \item the induced finite-nerve class
   22: \[
   23: \omega\in H^2(N(\mathcal U),A),
   24: \]
   25: obtained by identifying \v{C}ech cochains on $\mathcal U$ with simplicial cochains on the finite nerve, transporting the branch obstruction cocycle through that identification, and writing
   26: \[
   27: \omega:=\omega_v
   28: \]
   29: for the chosen global component section. When the class is also viewed as a derived
   30: $H^2$-class, the presentation includes either the
   31: \v{C}ech--derived comparison package of
   32: \Cref{def:cech-derived-comparison-package} or the finite good-cover Leray
   33: comparison of \Cref{lem:generated-subsite-model-interface}. Without one of
   34: these comparison inputs, \(\omega\) is only the selected finite-nerve
   35: \v{C}ech/simplicial class.
   36: \end{enumerate}
   37: Write
   38: \[
   39: \eta_A:H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)\longrightarrow \mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)
   40: \]
   41: for the map in the universal coefficient exact sequence
   42: \[
   43: 0\to \operatorname{Ext}^1(H_1(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)\to H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)\xrightarrow{\eta_A}\mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)\to 0
   44: \]
   45: \cite[Sec.~3.1]{Hatcher2002}, and define the \emph{homological evaluation map}
   46: \[
   47: \mathrm{ev}_{\omega}:=\eta_A(\omega).
   48: \]
   49: \end{definition}
   50: 
   51: \begin{definition}[Presentation-comparison groupoid]\label{def:finite-nerve-comparison-relation}
   52: For finite nerve representatives of a fixed component obstruction class, an
   53: \emph{elementary comparison} is one of the three operations listed in
   54: \Cref{prop:invariance-visible-quotients}: homology-equivalent refinement,
   55: cohomologous cocycle replacement, or re-trivialization of the constant band.
   56: The \emph{presentation-comparison groupoid} has these presentations as
   57: objects and finite zigzags of elementary comparisons and formal inverses as
   58: morphisms, with composition given by concatenation of zigzags. We say that two
   59: presentations are comparison-equivalent when they lie in the same connected
   60: component of this groupoid. Thus the comparison data carried by a finite
   61: zigzag are part of the pseudofunctorial assignment; no path independence
   62: between distinct zigzags is asserted unless an additional coherence
   63: hypothesis is imposed.
   64: \end{definition}
   65: 
   66: \begin{proposition}[Pseudofunctorial assignment of $K_\omega$ and $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^\omega$]\label{prop:invariance-visible-quotients}
   67: Let $(\mathcal U,A,\omega)$ and $(\mathcal U',A',\omega')$ be finite nerve representatives of the same component obstruction class. Suppose first that the two presentations differ by one of the following elementary comparisons:
   68: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
   69: \item refinement of the cover by a simplicial map
   70: \[
   71: f:N(\mathcal U')\to N(\mathcal U)
   72: \]
   73: from the refined nerve to the original nerve, such that
   74: \[
   75: \omega'=f^*\omega
   76: \]
   77: and
   78: \[
   79: f_*:H_2(N(\mathcal U'),\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\sim} H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)
   80: \]
   81: is an isomorphism, with the coefficient group fixed;
   82: \item replacement of the \v{C}ech cocycle by a cohomologous cocycle in $H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$;
   83: \item re-trivialization of the band by an isomorphism of coefficient groups
   84: \[
   85: \theta:A\xrightarrow{\sim} A',
   86: \]
   87: so that
   88: \[
   89: \omega'=\theta_*\omega.
   90: \]
   91: \end{enumerate}
   92: Then there exists a specified coefficient comparison isomorphism $\phi:A\to A'$---the identity in \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)}, and $\theta$ in \textup{(iii)}---such that
   93: \[
   94: \phi\bigl(K_{\omega}\bigr)=K_{\omega'}
   95: \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   96: \bar\phi:A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}=A/K_\omega\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/K_{\omega'}=A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega'}
   97: \]
   98: is the induced quotient isomorphism. In particular, both $K_{\omega}$ and $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}$ are transported by the three elementary comparison operations listed above, with the refinement direction fixed by the displayed pullback map.
   99: 
  100: More generally, if the two presentations are joined by a morphism $\Gamma$ in
  101: the presentation-comparison groupoid of
  102: \Cref{def:finite-nerve-comparison-relation}, then the chosen finite comparison
  103: zigzag $\Gamma$ determines, by composition of the elementary coefficient
  104: comparisons and their inverses, an isomorphism
  105: \[
  106: \phi_\Gamma:A\xrightarrow{\sim} A'
  107: \]
  108: such that
  109: \[
  110: \phi_\Gamma(K_\omega)=K_{\omega'}
  111: \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  112: A/K_\omega\xrightarrow{\sim}A'/K_{\omega'}
  113: \]
  114: is the corresponding composite quotient isomorphism. Hence
  115: $(\mathcal U,A,\omega)\mapsto (K_\omega\le A)$ and
  116: $(\mathcal U,A,\omega)\mapsto A_{\mathrm{vis}}^\omega$ define a pseudofunctorial assignment over the
  117: presentation-comparison groupoid. They are presentation-object canonical:
  118: once a finite nerve, coefficient trivialization, and comparison package have
  119: been fixed, the subgroup and quotient are determined by that object. Along a
  120: chosen comparison zigzag they are transported functorially by the displayed
  121: composite isomorphism. The statement does not assert path independence, and
  122: it does not identify the isomorphisms attached to two different zigzags with
  123: the same endpoints.
  124: \end{proposition}
  125: 
  126: \begin{remark}[Typical refinements]\label{rem:refinement-iso}
  127: The refinements used later are simplicial homotopy equivalences on the chosen nerves---for example, barycentric subdivisions and the standard refinements attached to good covers---and therefore satisfy the hypothesis of case \textup{(i)} of \Cref{prop:invariance-visible-quotients}.
  128: \end{remark}
  129: 
  130: \begin{remark}[Necessity of homology equivalences and chosen paths]\label{rem:homology-equality}
  131: The equalities in \Cref{prop:invariance-visible-quotients} rely on the assumption that the refinement map induces an isomorphism on $H_2$. Without that hypothesis, for a refinement \(f:N(\mathcal U')\to N(\mathcal U)\) with \(\omega'=f^*\omega\), naturality gives
  132: \[
  133: K_{\omega'}=\operatorname{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}\circ f_*)\subseteq K_{\omega}.
  134: \]
  135: Hence one obtains \(K_{\omega'}\subseteq K_{\omega}\), and therefore a comparison map
  136: \[
  137: A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega'}=A/K_{\omega'}\twoheadrightarrow
  138: A/K_{\omega}=A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega},
  139: \]
  140: but not equality. The term ``homological cokernel'' is therefore reserved for refinements and presentations that are homology-equivalent in this precise sense.
  141: 
  142: For presentations connected by several finite zigzags, the comparison
  143: isomorphism is part of the presentation-comparison groupoid. A different
  144: zigzag may compose the re-trivialization automorphisms of the coefficient band
  145: in a different way, and the paper does not quotient by that possible holonomy.
  146: Thus the assignment is pseudofunctorial over the presentation-comparison groupoid rather than a path-independent quotient
  147: on the set of comparison-equivalence classes.
  148: \end{remark}
  149: 
  150: \begin{proof}
  151: Case \textup{(ii)} is immediate because cohomologous cocycles define the same element of $H^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$ and hence have the same image under $\eta_A$. Here $\phi=\mathrm{id}_A$, so the quotient map is the identity on $A/K_\omega$.
  152: 
  153: In case \textup{(i)}, the assumption on $f$ gives an isomorphism on $H_2$. Since $\omega'=f^*(\omega)$ and the universal coefficient map is natural, one has
  154: \[
  155: \mathrm{ev}_{\omega'}=\eta_A\bigl(f^*(\omega)\bigr)=\eta_A(\omega)\circ f_*,
  156: \]
  157: where $f_*:H_2(N(\mathcal U'),\mathbb Z)\to H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ is induced on homology and is an isomorphism by hypothesis. Hence $\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega'})=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_\omega)$, so $K_{\omega'}=K_{\omega}$ and $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega'}\cong A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega}$.
  158: The comparison is canonical because the refinement operation supplies the direction of $f$ and hence the specified isomorphism $f_*$; replacing $f_*$ by its inverse would compare the evaluation maps in the wrong direction. Thus the subgroup equality occurs inside the same coefficient group $A$, and the quotient isomorphism is induced by $\phi=\mathrm{id}_A$.
  159: 
  160: In case \textup{(iii)}, the coefficient isomorphism $\theta$ identifies the two cohomology groups, and $\omega'=\theta_*(\omega)$. Naturality gives the coefficient-isomorphism square
  161: \[
  162: \begin{array}{ccc}
  163: H^2(N(\mathcal U),A) & \xrightarrow{\eta_A} &
  164: \mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A)\\
  165: \theta_*\downarrow\phantom{\theta_*} && \phantom{\theta\circ(-)}\downarrow\theta\circ(-)\\
  166: H^2(N(\mathcal U),A') & \xrightarrow{\eta_{A'}} &
  167: \mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),A'),
  168: \end{array}
  169: \]
  170: and hence
  171: \[
  172: \mathrm{ev}_{\omega'}=\eta_{A'}(\omega')=\eta_{A'}\bigl(\theta_*(\omega)\bigr)=\theta\circ \eta_A(\omega)=\theta\circ \mathrm{ev}_\omega.
  173: \]
  174: Therefore $K_{\omega'}=\theta(K_{\omega})$, and $\theta$ induces an isomorphism between $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^\omega$ and $A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega'}$.
  175: 
  176: In all three cases the induced quotient map is well defined because the chosen coefficient comparison $\phi$ sends $K_\omega$ onto $K_{\omega'}$. Its inverse is induced by the inverse coefficient comparison: the identity in cases \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)}, and $\theta^{-1}$ in case \textup{(iii)}. This proves functoriality of the specified elementary comparison and invariance of the quotient for that elementary morphism.
  177: 
  178: For a finite zigzag in the comparison groupoid, apply the elementary
  179: case at each step. If a step is traversed in the opposite direction, use the
  180: inverse coefficient and quotient isomorphisms just constructed. Composition of
  181: the finitely many subgroup identifications gives
  182: \[
  183: \phi_\Gamma(K_\omega)=K_{\omega'},
  184: \]
  185: and the universal property of quotients gives the displayed quotient
  186: isomorphism. Concatenating two zigzags concatenates the corresponding composite
  187: coefficient maps, so these assignments respect identity zigzags and composition
  188: of zigzags. Thus finite composites of the three comparison operations preserve
  189: the presentation-relative homological image subgroup and quotient in the stated
  190: groupoid-indexed sense.
  191: \end{proof}
  192: 
  193: \begin{proposition}[Finite nerve comparison isomorphism]\label{prop:finite-nerve-comparison}
  194: Work in one finite nerve representative
  195: $(\mathcal U,A,\omega)$ of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}; in
  196: particular, the band has been trivialized on $\mathcal U$ and is being
  197: viewed as the constant finite abelian group $A$ on the selected finite
  198: nerve. Use the total order on the finite index set $I$ already fixed in
  199: \Cref{def:ordered-cech-convention} for
  200: \[
  201: \mathcal U=\{a_i\to a\}_{i\in I}.
  202: \]
  203: Use the ordered \v{C}ech convention in which $\check C^n(\mathcal U,A)$
  204: is indexed by tuples
  205: \[
  206: i_0<\cdots<i_n
  207: \]
  208: with nonempty overlap, and use the corresponding ordered oriented
  209: simplices of $N(\mathcal U)$ for simplicial cochains. For each $n\ge 0$,
  210: each nonempty ordered $(n{+}1)$-fold overlap $a_{i_0\cdots i_n}$
  211: determines the oriented $n$-simplex $(i_0,\dots,i_n)$ of the selected
  212: nerve, and the assignment
  213: \[
  214: \Theta_{\mathcal U}^n:\check C^n(\mathcal U,A)\to C^n(N(\mathcal U),A),\qquad
  215: (\alpha_{i_0\cdots i_n})\longmapsto\bigl((i_0,\dots,i_n)\mapsto \alpha_{i_0\cdots i_n}\bigr)
  216: \]
  217: is an isomorphism of cochain groups. Under this correspondence,
  218: \[
  219: \delta\leftrightarrow d,\qquad
  220: B^n\leftrightarrow B^n,\qquad
  221: Z^n\leftrightarrow Z^n.
  222: \]
  223: Hence the \v{C}ech cohomology of this selected ordered finite nerve
  224: presentation with constant coefficients $A$ is identified with the
  225: simplicial cohomology of $N(\mathcal U)$ with coefficients in $A$.
  226: \end{proposition}
  227: \begin{proof}
  228: The hypotheses are part of the finite nerve representative: the cover is
  229: finite, the coefficient sheaf has been trivialized to the constant group
  230: $A$ on this cover, and the comparison is being made on the chosen finite
  231: nerve rather than on an arbitrary refinement system. With the fixed order
  232: on $I$, the $n$-cochains on $\mathcal U$ are families of coefficients
  233: indexed by nonempty ordered $(n{+}1)$-fold overlaps
  234: $a_{i_0\cdots i_n}$ with $i_0<\cdots<i_n$, while the simplicial
  235: $n$-cochains on $N(\mathcal U)$ are coefficient functions on the
  236: corresponding ordered oriented $n$-simplices $(i_0,\dots,i_n)$. By
  237: definition of the selected nerve, these two index sets agree, so
  238: $\Theta_{\mathcal U}^n$ is a bijection.
  239: 
  240: The \v{C}ech coboundary of $(\alpha_{i_0\cdots i_n})$ is the alternating
  241: sum obtained by omitting the $k$th ordered index, and the simplicial
  242: coboundary of $\Theta_{\mathcal U}^n(\alpha)$ uses the same ordered face
  243: map with the same sign $(-1)^k$. Since the coefficients are constant
  244: under the chosen trivialization, the restriction maps on coefficients are
  245: the identity maps of $A$. Because the face maps of $N(\mathcal U)$ are
  246: induced by omitting one ordered index, the two alternating sums coincide
  247: term by term. Hence
  248: \[
  249: \Theta_{\mathcal U}^{n+1}(\delta\alpha)=d(\Theta_{\mathcal U}^n(\alpha)).
  250: \]
  251: Therefore $\Theta_{\mathcal U}^\bullet$ is an isomorphism of cochain
  252: complexes, and it induces the stated identifications on cocycles,
  253: coboundaries, and cohomology. This is only the finite ordered
  254: constant-coefficient comparison used in \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation};
  255: promotion of a filtered \v{C}ech system to derived cohomology remains the
  256: separate \textup{(H4)} assumption of \Cref{rem:cech-vs-derived}.
  257: \end{proof}
  258: 
  259: \begin{proposition}[Strict versus presentation-relative homological image subgroups]\label{prop:strict-vs-intrinsic-hidden-subgroups}
  260: In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, let $\alpha\in Z^2(N(\mathcal U),A)$ be a simplicial cocycle representing $\omega$, and let
  261: \[
  262: \widetilde\alpha:C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A
  263: \]
  264: be the chain-level evaluation map obtained by linear extension from the oriented $2$-simplices. Then
  265: \[
  266: H_\alpha=\operatorname{Im}(\widetilde\alpha)
  267: \]
  268: and
  269: \[
  270: K_{\omega}:=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}).
  271: \]
  272: Thus $H_\alpha$ records presentation-level chain visibility: it is generated by the values of the chosen cocycle on all $2$-chains. By contrast, $K_{\omega}$ records cycle-level class visibility: it is the image that survives after passage to $2$-homology. In particular,
  273: \[
  274: K_{\omega}\subseteq H_\alpha.
  275: \]
  276: \end{proposition}
  277: \begin{proof}
  278: The image of $\widetilde\alpha$ is the subgroup generated by the values of $\alpha$ on the oriented $2$-simplices, equivalently by the values of the original \v{C}ech cocycle on the nonempty triple overlaps of $\mathcal U$. This is exactly the strict subgroup attached to the chosen presentation. The second equality is the definition of $K_\omega$. Since $H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$ is represented by $2$-cycles inside $C_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)$, every homological value counted by $\mathrm{ev}_\omega$ is, a fortiori, a chain-level value of $\widetilde\alpha$, so $K_\omega\subseteq H_\alpha$.
  279: \end{proof}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[

+ d(G)\leq 2\beta

+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}
