 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and

+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
+arbitrary empirical model.

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and
+$K_1+K_2=G$ if and only if
+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
+arbitrary empirical model.
 
-Our starting point is the extension chain
+The standard input is as follows.  We use universal satisfaction on nonempty
+teams of assignments, presheaves and their sheafifications, stackification of
+categories fibred in groupoids, the classification of banded gerbes by
+Giraud's $H^2$, the \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison on the specified Leray

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and
+$K_1+K_2=G$ if and only if
+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
+arbitrary empirical model.

+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and
+$K_1+K_2=G$ if and only if
+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
+arbitrary empirical model.

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and
+$K_1+K_2=G$ if and only if
+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
+arbitrary empirical model.

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and

+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta

+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.

+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. +\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. +A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf. When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[

+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and

+\[

+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary

+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 531: \item over each member $U_i$ of the cover there is the chosen local object $x_i$ with automorphism group $A$;
 532: \item the chosen transition maps have triple-overlap defect exactly $\alpha$;
 533: \item the presheaf of isomorphism classes satisfies
 534: \[
 535:  \pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\cong F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}.
 536: \]
 537: \end{enumerate}
 538: Thus the example begins with an explicit presheaf of local sections and then chooses local lift object and transition data realizing that functor; the component gerbe is recovered from those data by stackification rather than being taken as primitive input.
 539: 
 540: Let
 541: \[
 542: \mathfrak L_r:=a(\mathfrak P_r).
 543: \]
 544: Because $\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_r)\cong F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_a}$, the sheaf of connected components of $\mathfrak L_r$ has exactly one global section at $a$, represented by the constant compatible family above. Therefore
 545: \[
 546: \Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v\}.
 547: \]
 548: But $\alpha$ is nonzero, so the descent datum is ineffective and no object exists over $a$ in the resulting stack; equivalently, the unique component gerbe is non-neutral. Hence
 549: \[
 550: \mathfrak G_v=\mathfrak L_r,
 551: \qquad
 552: \omega_v=[\alpha]\neq 0.
 553: \]
 554: Combining this with the already computed presheaf-level facts gives
 555: \[
 556: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r),
 557: \qquad
 558: M,p\nVdash \Sec_s(r),
 559: \qquad
 560: \Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v\},
 561: \qquad
 562: \mathfrak G_v=\mathfrak L_r,
 563: \qquad
 564: \omega_v=[\alpha]\neq 0.
 565: \]
 566: The good cover $\mathcal U$ trivializes the constant band, all finite intersections are contractible, and therefore the $H^1$-vanishing and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses of \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction,def:finite-nerve-presentation} are satisfied.
 567: 
 568: Since
 569: \[
 570: H_1(N,\mathbb Z) = 0,
 571: \qquad
 572: H_2(N,\mathbb Z) \cong \mathbb Z
 573: \]
 574: \cite[Secs.~2.1, 2.2]{Hatcher2002}, the universal coefficient theorem gives
 575: \[
 576: H^2(N, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})
 577: \cong
 578: \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})
 579: \cong
 580: \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}.
 581: \]
 582: Let $\omega$ be the nonzero class, and let $[S^2]$ denote the fundamental class in $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)$. Then
 583: \[
 584: \mathrm{ev}_\omega([S^2]) = 1 \in \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z},
 585: \]
 586: so the homological evaluation map is surjective. By \Cref{cor:maximal-collapse},
 587: \[
 588: K_\omega = A = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z},
 589: \qquad
 590: Q_\omega = 0.
 591: \]
 592: Hence
 593: \[
 594: M,p\Vdash \NoAmalg_s(r),
 595: \qquad
 596: \omega=\omega_v\neq 0,
 597: \qquad
 598: \mathrm{ev}_{\omega}:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\twoheadrightarrow A,
 599: \qquad
 600: K_\omega=A,
 601: \qquad
 602: Q_\omega=0.
 603: \]
 604: Since $K_\omega = A$, \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient} gives
 605: \[
 606: X_\omega = \mathrm{Ann}(K_\omega) = \mathrm{Ann}(A) = \{1\},
 607: \]
 608: so only the trivial character is class-admissible. Equivalently, $Q_\omega = A/K_\omega = 0$.
 609: 
 610: This example therefore verifies the full downstream hypothesis chain
 611: \[
 612: (\mathcal C_a,\mathfrak P_r,A,\omega,\mathrm{ev}_\omega,K_\omega,Q_\omega)
 613: \]
 614: inside a concrete site-theoretic example, once the realization stack has been fixed by the chosen cocycle data. It is the opposite extreme from the $\mathbb{R}P^2$ blind case of \Cref{ex:rp2-character-blind}: for an $\mathbb{R}P^2$-type nerve one has $K_\omega=0$, every character is class-admissible, and the obstruction is entirely in the UCT $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ kernel with $Q_\omega=A$; for the present $S^2$-type nerve one has $K_\omega=A$, only the trivial character is class-admissible, and the obstruction is purely $H_2$-type with $Q_\omega=0$.
 615: \end{example}

 617: \begin{definition}[Auxiliary register for the homological quotient]\label{def:intrinsic-strictification-code}
 618: An \emph{auxiliary register for the homological quotient} for the obstruction class $\omega$ consists of a finite set $R$ and an injective map
 619: \[
 620: \iota_{\omega}:A\hookrightarrow Q_{\omega}\times R
 621: \]
 622: such that
 623: \[
 624: \mathrm{pr}_1\circ\iota_{\omega}=\pi_{\omega}.
 625: \]
 626: \end{definition}
 627: 
 628: \begin{corollary}[Intrinsic hidden-state lower bound]\label{cor:intrinsic-hidden-state-lower-bound}
 629: Every auxiliary register for the homological quotient satisfies
 630: \[
 631: |R|\ge |K_{\omega}|.
 632: \]
 633: Equivalently,
 634: \[
 635: \log_2|R|\ge \log_2|K_{\omega}|.
 636: \]
 637: This lower bound is sharp.
 638: \end{corollary}
 639: 
 640: \begin{proof}
 641: By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, the fibers of $\pi_{\omega}$ are exactly the cosets of $K_{\omega}$, so every fiber has cardinality $|K_{\omega}|$. The same fiber-counting argument as in \Cref{thm:minimal-information-cost-of-strictification} therefore shows that any injective code preserving the first projection must satisfy $|R|\ge |K_{\omega}|$.
 642: 
 643: For sharpness, take $R:=K_{\omega}$ and choose a set-theoretic section $s_{\omega}:Q_{\omega}\to A$ of $\pi_{\omega}$. Then
 644: \[
 645: \iota_{\omega}(x):=\bigl(\pi_{\omega}(x),x-s_{\omega}(\pi_{\omega}(x))\bigr)
 646: \]
 647: is injective.
 648: \end{proof}

 650: \begin{theorem}[Prime decomposition of homology-evaluation quotient and budget]\label{thm:intrinsic-prime-decomposition}
 651: Write the finite abelian group $A$ as a direct sum of its $p$-primary components:
 652: \[
 653: A=\bigoplus_p A_{(p)}.
 654: \]
 655: Let $\omega_p\in H^2(N(\mathcal U),A_{(p)})$ be the image of $\omega$ under the projection onto the $p$-primary summand. Then
 656: \[
 657: \mathrm{ev}_{\omega}=\bigoplus_p \mathrm{ev}_{\omega_p},
 658: \qquad
 659: K_{\omega}=\bigoplus_p K_{\omega,p},
 660: \qquad
 661: Q_{\omega}\cong \bigoplus_p A_{(p)}/K_{\omega,p},
 662: \]
 663: where
 664: \[
 665: K_{\omega,p}:=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega_p}).
 666: \]
 667: Consequently,
 668: \[
 669: |K_{\omega}|=\prod_p |K_{\omega,p}|,
 670: \qquad
 671: \log_2|K_{\omega}|=\sum_p \log_2|K_{\omega,p}|.
 672: \]
 673: \end{theorem}
 674: 
 675: \begin{proof}
 676: Both $H^2(N(\mathcal U),-)$ and $\mathrm{Hom}(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z),-)$ commute with finite direct sums, so the universal coefficient map is compatible with the primary decomposition of $A$. Hence
 677: \[
 678: \eta_A(\omega)=\bigoplus_p \eta_{A_{(p)}}(\omega_p),
 679: \]
 680: which is exactly the asserted decomposition of $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}$.
 681: 
 682: Taking images gives
 683: \[
 684: K_{\omega}
 685: =
 686: \mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})
 687: =
 688: \bigoplus_p \mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega_p})
 689: =
 690: \bigoplus_p K_{\omega,p},
 691: \]
 692: by \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}. The quotient decomposition follows immediately:
 693: \[
 694: Q_{\omega}
 695: =
 696: A/K_{\omega}
 697: \cong
 698: \bigoplus_p A_{(p)}/K_{\omega,p}.
 699: \]
 700: Since finite direct sums correspond to products of cardinalities, the budget formula is immediate.
 701: \end{proof}
 702: 
 703: \begin{corollary}[Intrinsic budget versus strict budget]\label{cor:strict-intrinsic-budget-comparison}
 704: For every finite \v{C}ech cocycle representative $\alpha$ of the class $\omega$,
 705: \[
 706: |K_{\omega}|\le |H_\alpha|,
 707: \qquad
 708: \log_2|K_{\omega}|\le \log_2|H_\alpha|.
 709: \]
 710: Hence the presentation-relative minimum auxiliary register size never exceeds the strict presentation-level budget. Equality holds if and only if the canonical surjection
 711: \[
 712: Q_{\omega}\twoheadrightarrow A/H_\alpha
 713: \]
 714: is an isomorphism.
 715: \end{corollary}
 716: 
 717: \begin{proof}
 718: By \Cref{cor:strict-to-intrinsic-visible}, there is a surjective homomorphism
 719: \[
 720: Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}\twoheadrightarrow A/H_\alpha.
 721: \]
 722: For finite groups this implies
 723: \[
 724: |A|/|K_{\omega}|\ge |A|/|H_\alpha|,
 725: \]
 726: hence $|K_{\omega}|\le |H_\alpha|$. The logarithmic inequality is immediate. Equality of cardinalities holds exactly when the displayed surjection is bijective.
 727: \end{proof}
 728: 
 729: \begin{corollary}[Maximal collapse criterion]\label{cor:maximal-collapse}
 730: In the setting of \Cref{def:finite-nerve-presentation}, the following are equivalent:
 731: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
 732: \item $\mathrm{ev}_{\omega}:H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\to A$ is surjective;
 733: \item $K_{\omega}=A$;
 734: \item $Q_{\omega}=0$;
 735: \item the intrinsic logarithmic fibre cardinality is maximal:
 736: \[
 737: \log_2|K_{\omega}|=\log_2|A|.
 738: \]
 739: \end{enumerate}
 740: \end{corollary}
 741: 
 742: \begin{proof}
 743: By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, $K_{\omega}=\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_{\omega})$, so \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} are equivalent. Condition \textup{(ii)} is equivalent to \textup{(iii)} by the definition of $Q_{\omega}=A/K_{\omega}$. For finite groups, \textup{(ii)} is also equivalent to $|K_{\omega}|=|A|$, which is exactly \textup{(iv)} after taking $\log_2$.
 744: \end{proof}
