+We now describe the framework.  An information state
+$p=(\Gamma_p,R_p)$ is a nonempty team $R_p$ of assignments with common finite
+context $\Gamma_p$.  We write $M,p\Vdash\varphi$ when every assignment in
+$R_p$ satisfies $\varphi$ in the ordinary Tarskian sense.  Thus $\Vdash$ is
+universal team satisfaction, not set-theoretic, Kripke, Beth, or
+Kripke--Joyal forcing.  Refinement enlarges the context and may restrict the
+team, which immediately gives persistence.  Point assignments enter through
+the singleton-state embedding.  The later semantic frameworks add typed data
+while preserving the truth of formulas in the reduct; we call these
+truth-preserving reduct expansions, rather than conservative extensions,
+because consequence conservativity is not asserted without an expansion
+theorem for every lower model.
 
-The second part begins once the set-valued local-object functor is enriched by groupoid-valued data. \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity} gives a rigidity statement for representative-rigid lifts: if the local-object presheaf is slice-separated and a realization prestack admits a strict functorial choice of representatives and is globally conservative at the terminal fibre, then the sheafification unit is surjective there; under $H^1$-vanishing and the same slice-separatedness, this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf at the terminal fibre. Thus gluing-level nullity is necessarily tied to genuinely gluing-sensitive lift data. \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} identifies the canonicity that survives at this level: once the sheafified local object functor has been lifted to a banded realization stack, the branch obstruction map to derived $H^2$ is intrinsic up to equivalence of banded extensions. For such an extension, visible value classes are the global sections of the sheaf of connected components (\Cref{thm:visible-value-components}), each visible branch determines a banded component gerbe (\Cref{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}), and, on slice-separated reference slices, \Cref{thm:gerbe-null-semantics} identifies gluing-level absence with the existence of visible branches together with non-neutrality of the corresponding component gerbes.
+For an admissible parameter $r$ at $p$, the paper specifies a thin
+reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$, its base object

+$F_{p,s}:\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.  A matching family
+without an element of $F_{p,s}(a)$ is the set-valued failure studied here.

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. +The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. +\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. +The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

   1: \section{Comparison of branches and realization}\label{sec:branch-aggregation}
   2: 
   3: We compare the quotients attached to the different global component sections of a single admissible parameter. Retaining the component label leads to a label-aware quotient, while forgetting it leads to a common-character quotient. The comparison results below are formal once the family of componentwise homological image subgroups have been fixed, whereas the construction theorems later in the section remain internal to explicitly chosen finite nerves and constant bands.
   4: 
   5: \begin{definition}[Family of componentwise homological image subgroups]\label{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}
   6: Fix an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ at a state $p$, and assume:
   7: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
   8: \item the hypotheses of \Cref{def:cech-gluing-obstruction} hold;
   9: \item the set $\Vis_{p,s}(r)$ is finite and nonempty;
  10: \item every component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ is banded by the same finite abelian group $A$ and admits a finite nerve representative of its component obstruction class $\omega_v$.
  11: \end{enumerate}
  12: For each global component section $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$, write
  13: \[
  14: K_v:=K_{\omega_v},
  15: \qquad
  16: A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v:=A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\omega_v}=A/K_v,
  17: \qquad
  18: \pi_v:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v.
  19: \]
  20: \end{definition}
  21: 
  22: \begin{theorem}[Label-aware quotient]\label{thm:branch-sensitive-visible-quotient}
  23: In the setting of \Cref{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}, consider the diagonal map
  24: \[
  25: \Delta_{\mathrm{br}}:A\longrightarrow \prod_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v,
  26: \qquad
  27: x\longmapsto (\pi_v(x))_v.
  28: \]
  29: Then
  30: \[
  31: \ker(\Delta_{\mathrm{br}})=\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
  32: \]
  33: Consequently, the quotient
  34: \[
  35: A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r):=A\Big/\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v
  36: \]
  37: is canonically isomorphic to $\mathrm{Im}(\Delta_{\mathrm{br}})$. It is the maximal quotient of $A$ that remains visible once the component label itself is allowed as part of the semantic context.
  38: \end{theorem}
  39: 
  40: \begin{proof}
  41: For $x\in A$ one has $\Delta_{\mathrm{br}}(x)=0$ if and only if $\pi_v(x)=0$ for every global component section $v$, which is equivalent to $x\in K_v$ for every $v$. Hence
  42: \[
  43: \ker(\Delta_{\mathrm{br}})=\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
  44: \]
  45: The first isomorphism theorem therefore yields
  46: \[
  47: \mathrm{Im}(\Delta_{\mathrm{br}})
  48: \cong
  49: A\Big/\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
  50: \]
  51: Thus, once the global component section is known, two elements of $A$ remain semantically indistinguishable exactly when they are indistinguishable on every individual branch quotient.
  52: \end{proof}
  53: 
  54: \begin{theorem}[Common-character quotient]\label{thm:branch-uniform-visible-quotient}
  55: In the setting of \Cref{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}, let
  56: \[
  57: X_v:=\{\chi\in \widehat A\mid \chi_*(\omega_v)=0\}
  58: \]
  59: for each global component section $v$, and define the common annihilating characters by
  60: \[
  61: X^{\mathrm{unif}}(r):=\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} X_v.
  62: \]
  63: Then
  64: \[
  65: X^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)=\mathrm{Ann}\Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr).
  66: \]
  67: Consequently, the quotient
  68: \[
  69: A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r):=A\Big/\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v
  70: \]
  71: is exactly the quotient detected by the characters that are admissible on every global component section simultaneously.
  72: \end{theorem}
  73: 
  74: \begin{proof}
  75: By \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, one has
  76: \[
  77: X_v=\mathrm{Ann}(K_v)
  78: \]
  79: for every $v$. Therefore
  80: \[
  81: X^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)
  82: =
  83: \bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} \mathrm{Ann}(K_v)
  84: =
  85: \mathrm{Ann}\Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr),
  86: \]
  87: where the last identity is the standard annihilator formula for finite abelian groups \cite[Part~I, Chap.~2]{Terras1999}. Finite abelian duality then gives
  88: \[
  89: \bigcap_{\chi\in X^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)} \ker\chi
  90: =
  91: \sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
  92: \]
  93: Hence the quotient detected by all common annihilating characters is precisely
  94: \[
  95: A\Big/\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v.
  96: \qedhere
  97: \]
  98: \end{proof}
  99: 
 100: \begin{definition}[Canonical component-comparison map and resolution kernel]\label{def:branch-comparison-map}
 101: In the setting of \Cref{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}, let
 102: \[
 103: \pi_{\mathrm{br}}:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)
 104: \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 105: \pi_{\mathrm{unif}}:A\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)
 106: \]
 107: be the canonical quotient maps. Since
 108: \[
 109: \bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v
 110: \subseteq
 111: \sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v,
 112: \]
 113: there is a unique surjective homomorphism
 114: \[
 115: \beta_r:A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\twoheadrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)
 116: \]
 117: such that
 118: \[
 119: \beta_r\circ \pi_{\mathrm{br}}=\pi_{\mathrm{unif}}.
 120: \]
 121: Its kernel is denoted
 122: \[
 123: B_{\mathrm{res}}(r):=
 124: \ker(\beta_r)
 125: \cong
 126: \Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr)
 127: \]
 128: and called the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}.
 129: \end{definition}
 130: 
 131: \begin{theorem}[Exact comparison of label-aware and common-character visibility]\label{thm:branch-comparison-exact-sequence}
 132: In the setting of \Cref{def:branch-comparison-map}, there is a short exact sequence
 133: \[
 134: 0\longrightarrow B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)\longrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\xrightarrow{\ \beta_r\ } A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)\longrightarrow 0.
 135: \]
 136: Equivalently,
 137: \[
 138: \ker(\beta_r)
 139: \cong
 140: \Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\Bigr).
 141: \]
 142: Thus the precise gap between label-aware and common-character visibility is measured by the lattice interval from $\bigcap_v K_v$ to $\sum_v K_v$.
 143: \end{theorem}
 144: 
 145: \begin{proof}
 146: Existence and uniqueness of $\beta_r$ follow from the universal property of the quotient because
 147: \[
 148: \bigcap_v K_v\subseteq \sum_v K_v.
 149: \]
 150: Surjectivity is immediate from surjectivity of $\pi_{\mathrm{unif}}$. By the third isomorphism theorem,
 151: \[
 152: \ker(\beta_r)
 153: \cong
 154: \Bigl(\sum_v K_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_v K_v\Bigr),
 155: \]
 156: which gives the claimed exact sequence.
 157: \end{proof}
 158: 
 159: \begin{corollary}[Criterion for the absence of branch gain]\label{cor:no-branch-gain-criterion}
 160: In the setting of \Cref{def:branch-comparison-map}, the following are equivalent:
 161: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
 162: \item $\beta_r$ is an isomorphism;
 163: \item $B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)=0$;
 164: \item
 165: \[
 166: \bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v
 167: =
 168: \sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v;
 169: \]
 170: \item the homological image subgroups are branch-constant:
 171: \[
 172: K_v=K_w
 173: \qquad
 174: (\forall v,w\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)).
 175: \]
 176: \end{enumerate}
 177: Hence branch sensitivity yields no additional visible information exactly when all global component sections have the same presentation-relative homological image subgroup.
 178: \end{corollary}
 179: 
 180: \begin{proof}
 181: The equivalence of \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} is exactness of the sequence in \Cref{thm:branch-comparison-exact-sequence}. Condition \textup{(ii)} is equivalent to \textup{(iii)} by the quotient description of $B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)$.
 182: 
 183: If \textup{(iii)} holds, write the common subgroup as $H$. Then
 184: \[
 185: H=\bigcap_v K_v\subseteq K_v\subseteq \sum_v K_v=H
 186: \]
 187: for every global component section $v$, so each $K_v=H$, proving \textup{(iv)}. Conversely, if all $K_v$ are equal to one subgroup $H$, then clearly
 188: \[
 189: \bigcap_v K_v=H=\sum_v K_v.
 190: \qedhere
 191: \]
 192: \end{proof}
 193: 
 194: \begin{corollary}[Dual character description of the component-forgetting kernel]\label{cor:branch-resolution-dual}
 195: In the setting of \Cref{def:branch-comparison-map},
 196: \[
 197: \widehat{A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)}
 198: \cong
 199: \sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} X_v,
 200: \qquad
 201: \widehat{A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)}
 202: \cong
 203: \bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} X_v.
 204: \]
 205: Moreover,
 206: \[
 207: \widehat{B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)}
 208: \cong
 209: \Bigl(\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} X_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} X_v\Bigr).
 210: \]
 211: Thus the characters created by branch resolution are exactly the channels that belong to the subgroup generated by the componentwise admissible characters but fail to be uniformly admissible.
 212: \end{corollary}
 213: 
 214: \begin{proof}
 215: By \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, one has
 216: \[
 217: X_v=\mathrm{Ann}(K_v)
 218: \]
 219: for every global component section $v$. Finite abelian duality then gives
 220: \[
 221: \widehat{A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)}
 222: \cong
 223: \mathrm{Ann}\Bigl(\bigcap_v K_v\Bigr)
 224: =
 225: \sum_v \mathrm{Ann}(K_v)
 226: =
 227: \sum_v X_v
 228: \]
 229: and, by \Cref{thm:branch-uniform-visible-quotient},
 230: \[
 231: \widehat{A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)}
 232: \cong
 233: \bigcap_v X_v.
 234: \]
 235: Dualizing the short exact sequence of \Cref{thm:branch-comparison-exact-sequence} yields an exact sequence
 236: \[
 237: 0\longrightarrow \widehat{A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)}
 238: \longrightarrow \widehat{A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)}
 239: \longrightarrow \widehat{B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)}
 240: \longrightarrow 0,
 241: \]
 242: and substituting the two identifications above gives the claimed quotient description of $\widehat{B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)}$.
 243: \end{proof}

 245: \begin{definition}[Auxiliary register for the component-forgetting map]\label{def:branch-resolution-code}
 246: In the setting of \Cref{def:branch-comparison-map}, a \emph{auxiliary register for the component-forgetting map} consists of a finite set $R$ and an injective map
 247: \[
 248: \iota_{\mathrm{res}}:A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\hookrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)\times R
 249: \]
 250: such that
 251: \[
 252: \mathrm{pr}_1\circ \iota_{\mathrm{res}}=\beta_r.
 253: \]
 254: \end{definition}
 255: 
 256: \begin{theorem}[Exact logarithmic component-forgetting fibre cardinality]\label{thm:branch-resolution-budget}
 257: Every auxiliary register for the component-forgetting map satisfies
 258: \[
 259: |R|\ge |B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)|
 260: =
 261: \left|\Bigl(\sum_v K_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_v K_v\Bigr)\right|.
 262: \]
 263: Equivalently,
 264: \[
 265: \log_2|R|
 266: \ge
 267: \log_2|B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)|.
 268: \]
 269: This bound is sharp.
 270: \end{theorem}
 271: 
 272: \begin{proof}
 273: Since $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ \iota_{\mathrm{res}}=\beta_r$, every fiber of $\beta_r$ injects into $R$. By \Cref{thm:branch-comparison-exact-sequence}, each fiber of $\beta_r$ is a coset of $B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)$ and therefore has cardinality $|B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)|$. Hence
 274: \[
 275: |R|\ge |B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)|.
 276: \]
 277: 
 278: For sharpness, choose a finite set $R$ with
 279: \[
 280: |R|=|B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)|.
 281: \]
 282: Choose a set-theoretic section
 283: \[
 284: s:A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)\to A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)
 285: \]
 286: of $\beta_r$, and choose an injection
 287: \[
 288: j:B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)\hookrightarrow R.
 289: \]
 290: Define
 291: \[
 292: \iota_{\mathrm{res}}(x):=
 293: \bigl(\beta_r(x),j(x-s(\beta_r(x)))\bigr).
 294: \]
 295: Since $x-s(\beta_r(x))\in \ker(\beta_r)=B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)$, the map is well defined. If
 296: \[
 297: \iota_{\mathrm{res}}(x)=\iota_{\mathrm{res}}(y),
 298: \]
 299: then $\beta_r(x)=\beta_r(y)$ and
 300: \[
 301: j(x-s(\beta_r(x)))=j(y-s(\beta_r(y))).
 302: \]
 303: Injectivity of $j$ gives $x=y$, so $\iota_{\mathrm{res}}$ is injective and the bound is attained.
 304: \end{proof}
 305: 
 306: \begin{corollary}[Factorization of uniform quotient-fibre information]\label{cor:uniform-hidden-budget-factorization}
 307: In the setting of \Cref{def:branch-comparison-map},
 308: \[
 309: \left|\sum_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\right|
 310: =
 311: |B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)|
 312: \cdot
 313: \left|\bigcap_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_v\right|.
 314: \]
 315: Equivalently,
 316: \[
 317: \log_2\left|\sum_v K_v\right|
 318: =
 319: \log_2|B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)|
 320: +
 321: \log_2\left|\bigcap_v K_v\right|.
 322: \]
 323: Thus the minimum auxiliary register size behind uniform visibility factors exactly into a branch-resolution term and a residual within-branch hidden term.
 324: \end{corollary}
 325: 
 326: \begin{proof}
 327: By \Cref{def:branch-comparison-map},
 328: \[
 329: |B_{\mathrm{res}}(r)|
 330: =
 331: \left|\Bigl(\sum_v K_v\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(\bigcap_v K_v\Bigr)\right|
 332: =
 333: \frac{|\sum_v K_v|}{|\bigcap_v K_v|}.
 334: \]
 335: Rearranging gives the first displayed identity, and the second follows after taking base-$2$ logarithms.
 336: \end{proof}

 338: \begin{definition}[Common auxiliary register for the componentwise quotient maps]\label{def:branch-preserving-strictification-code}
 339: In the setting of \Cref{def:branchwise-intrinsic-data}, a \emph{common auxiliary register for the componentwise quotient maps} consists of a finite set $R$ and, for each global component section $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$, an injective map
 340: \[
 341: \iota_v:A\hookrightarrow A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v\times R
 342: \]
 343: such that
 344: \[
 345: \mathrm{pr}_1\circ \iota_v=\pi_v.
 346: \]
 347: \end{definition}
 348: 
 349: \begin{theorem}[Common-register fibre cardinality]\label{thm:multi-branch-strictification-budget}
 350: Every common auxiliary register for the componentwise quotient maps satisfies
 351: \[
 352: |R|\ge \max_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} |K_v|.
 353: \]
 354: Equivalently,
 355: \[
 356: \log_2|R|\ge \max_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} \log_2|K_v|.
 357: \]
 358: This bound is sharp.
 359: \end{theorem}
 360: 
 361: \begin{proof}
 362: Fix a global component section $v$. Since $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ \iota_v=\pi_v$, every fiber of $\pi_v$ injects into $R$. By \Cref{def:intrinsic-visible-quotient}, every fiber of $\pi_v$ is a coset of $K_v$ and hence has cardinality $|K_v|$. Therefore $|R|\ge |K_v|$ for every $v$, which proves the lower bound.
 363: 
 364: For sharpness, choose a finite set $R$ with
 365: \[
 366: |R|=\max_{v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} |K_v|.
 367: \]
 368: For each $v$, choose an injection
 369: \[
 370: j_v:K_v\hookrightarrow R
 371: \]
 372: and a set-theoretic section
 373: \[
 374: s_v:A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v\to A
 375: \]
 376: of $\pi_v$. Define
 377: \[
 378: \iota_v(x):=\bigl(\pi_v(x),j_v(x-s_v(\pi_v(x)))\bigr).
 379: \]
 380: Since $x-s_v(\pi_v(x))\in K_v$, the formula is well defined. If $\iota_v(x)=\iota_v(y)$, then $\pi_v(x)=\pi_v(y)$ and
 381: \[
 382: j_v(x-s_v(\pi_v(x)))=j_v(y-s_v(\pi_v(y))).
 383: \]
 384: Injectivity of $j_v$ gives $x=y$. Thus each $\iota_v$ is injective, so the bound is attained.
 385: \end{proof}
 386: 
 387: \begin{corollary}[Single-component reduction]\label{cor:single-branch-reduction}
 388: If
 389: \[
 390: \Vis_{p,s}(r)=\{v\},
 391: \]
 392: then
 393: \[
 394: A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\cong A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)\cong A_{\mathrm{vis}}^v
 395: \]
 396: and the optimal branch-preserving logarithmic fibre cardinality is exactly $|K_v|$.
 397: \end{corollary}
 398: 
 399: \begin{proof}
 400: If there is only one global component section, then
 401: \[
 402: \bigcap_{u\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_u
 403: =
 404: \sum_{u\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)} K_u
 405: =
 406: K_v.
 407: \]
 408: The quotient statements follow from \Cref{thm:branch-sensitive-visible-quotient,thm:branch-uniform-visible-quotient}, and the budget statement is \Cref{thm:multi-branch-strictification-budget}.
 409: \end{proof}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and
+$K_1+K_2=G$ if and only if
+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
+arbitrary empirical model.

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and
+$K_1+K_2=G$ if and only if
+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
+arbitrary empirical model.

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and
+$K_1+K_2=G$ if and only if
+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
+arbitrary empirical model.

+teams of assignments, presheaves and their sheafifications, stackification of

-The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. +We now describe the framework.  An information state
+$p=(\Gamma_p,R_p)$ is a nonempty team $R_p$ of assignments with common finite
+context $\Gamma_p$.  We write $M,p\Vdash\varphi$ when every assignment in
+$R_p$ satisfies $\varphi$ in the ordinary Tarskian sense.  Thus $\Vdash$ is

+Kripke--Joyal forcing.  Refinement enlarges the context and may restrict the

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. -The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. +\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{document}
 
 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite

+\[

+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology

-The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. +We now describe the framework.  An information state
+$p=(\Gamma_p,R_p)$ is a nonempty team $R_p$ of assignments with common finite
+context $\Gamma_p$.  We write $M,p\Vdash\varphi$ when every assignment in
+$R_p$ satisfies $\varphi$ in the ordinary Tarskian sense.  Thus $\Vdash$ is
+universal team satisfaction, not set-theoretic, Kripke, Beth, or
+Kripke--Joyal forcing.  Refinement enlarges the context and may restrict the

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. +The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. +\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}
