 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and
+$K_1+K_2=G$ if and only if
+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
+arbitrary empirical model.

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

\section{Concluding remarks}\label{sec:conclusion}

The paper separates three stages of the local-to-global problem. At the level of information states, \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} shows that existence of a matching family and matching without amalgamation are invisible in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment considered here. This is not intended as a general expressivity theorem, but it does isolate the first place at which the local-object layer goes beyond the lower team-satisfaction language.

At the passage from set-valued to groupoid-valued data, \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity} shows that a slice-separated representative-rigid lift can be globally conservative only when the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre is surjective; under $H^1$-vanishing and separatedness on the slice on the slice site associated to the parameter, this is equivalent to sheafiness of the presheaf of local sections at that fibre. Thus the gerbe-theoretic part of the theory is necessarily relative to additional lift data. \Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface} makes this limitation exact for finite empirical models: their support presheaves have canonical refinement-functorial split realization stacks with neutral component gerbes. The AMB class is instead the degree-one class of a torsor indexed by a local section, and cannot be recovered for all finite models by the componentwise Giraud map, whose domain is empty for strongly contextual models. Once a non-split banded extension is separately supplied, \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} gives the maximal remaining canonicity: the component obstruction class is intrinsic up to equivalence of such extensions.

For a finite abelian component obstruction class, the presentation-object
subgroup \(K_\omega=\operatorname{Im}(\mathrm{ev}_\omega)\) and quotient
\(A_{\mathrm{vis}}^\omega=A/K_\omega\) capture the homological information
that survives at a fixed finite nerve representative; across presentations
they form a groupoid-indexed invariant transported along chosen morphisms in
the presentation-comparison groupoid. The componentwise comparison sequence and
the construction theorems show how these quotients behave when several
global component sections are present, under the fixed finite nerve, constant-band,
explicit \v{C}ech--derived comparison package, and \(H_1=0\) hypotheses used
in the construction. When in addition
\(H_2(N(\mathcal U),\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta\), the realizable hidden
subgroups are exactly the subgroups generated by at most \(\beta\) elements.
The bouquet construction supplies an explicit chosen class of good-cover
examples in which the two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroupss can be described
completely: the nonzero finite abelian groups that occur are exactly those
with \(d(G)\le2\beta\) which are not cyclic \(p\)-groups. This does not
transfer to bare empirical models, whose canonical split lift has zero hidden
subgroups. The appendix
contains only supplementary material: the refinement-dynamic extension,
finite-state complexity bounds, and the GHZ/Mermin lift used as an
illustrative chosen datum.

The hypothesis package is therefore deliberately visible: \textup{(RC)} for
local objects, \textup{(H1)}--\textup{(H4)} and global conservativity for
component gerbes, separatedness on the slice whenever global component sections are used as
strict compatible local sections, separatedness on the slice and $H^1$-vanishing for
terminal-fibre rigidity, and finite-nerve plus constant-band data together
with the explicit \v{C}ech--derived comparison package for homological
visibility.
This paper keeps that package in the pullback-based slice-site formulation; the
meet-semilattice presentation belongs to the companion APAL article. The
comparison between presentations is consequently groupoid-indexed and
zigzag-dependent, not a claim of presentation-free canonical representatives.

\subsection{The exact interface with empirical models}

Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models already have two categorical
reformulations close to the question considered here. Car\`u identifies the
degree-one cohomology used by Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa with torsors
trivialized by the measurement cover \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}. More recently,
Barbosa, Kharoof, and Okay construct fully faithful functors from measurement
scenarios to bundle and simplicial-bundle scenarios, together with natural
isomorphisms on their empirical-model functors
\cite{BarbosaKharoofOkay2024}. Neither construction produces a banded gerbe
or a banded stack lift in the sense of
\Cref{def:realization-stack-extension}. The following comparison locates the
gap precisely.

Let a \emph{finite measurement scenario} be a finite set \(X\), finite
nonempty outcome sets \(O_x\) for \(x\in X\), and a finite antichain
\(\mathcal M\) of subsets of \(X\) whose union is \(X\). Write
\(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}\) for the finite context category consisting of
the subcontexts of members of \(\mathcal M\), with inclusions as arrows, and
equip it with the coverage induced by the maximal contexts. We also use its
terminal augmentation, obtained by adjoining \(X\) and declaring
\(\mathcal M\) to cover \(X\). A finite empirical model
\[
e=(e_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}
\]
is a compatible family of probability distributions on
\(\prod_{x\in C}O_x\). Its support presheaf is
\[
S_e(U)=\operatorname{supp}(e_U)
\qquad(U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}),
\]
where compatibility makes the marginal \(e_U\) independent of the maximal
context containing \(U\) \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011}. At the adjoined
terminal object we take the right Kan extension
\[
\widehat S_e(X):=
\varprojlim_{U\in\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}}S_e(U).
\]
Thus an element of \(\widehat S_e(X)\) is, by definition, a compatible family
of supported local assignments. Below \(aS_e\) denotes the sheafification of
this terminally augmented presheaf.

A \emph{context refinement} used below is a refinement
\(\rho:\mathcal M'\to\mathcal M\) on the same measurements and outcomes,
with \(C'\subseteq\rho(C')\), for which marginalization defines the refined
model \(\rho^*e\). The inclusion of downward-closed context categories induces
a functor
\[
u_\rho:\mathcal D_{\mathcal M'}\hookrightarrow
\mathcal D_{\mathcal M}
\]
which is required to be continuous for the two generated cover topologies and
to extend to their terminal augmentations. We also require the natural
base-change isomorphism
\[
S_{\rho^*e}\cong u_\rho^*S_e.
\]
This includes ordinary iterated refinements which are covering refinements
for the generated topology. No
claim is made here for resource-theoretic simulations which change the
measurement or outcome sets.

\begin{proposition}[Abramsky--Brandenburger support interface]\label{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}
For every finite empirical model \(e\), the following sets are naturally in
bijection:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item compatible families \((s_C)_{C\in\mathcal M}\) with
      \(s_C\in S_e(C)\);
\item global assignments \(s\in\prod_{x\in X}O_x\) such that
      \(s|_C\in S_e(C)\) for every \(C\in\mathcal M\);
\item global sections of the support presheaf in the standard
      Abramsky--Brandenburger sense;
\item elements of \(\widehat S_e(X)\), equivalently elements of
      \((aS_e)(X)\) on the terminally augmented context site.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, if both \(\CompSec_s(r)\) and \(\Sec_s(r)\) are interpreted
from this same support presheaf on the standard measurement cover, then
\[
M,p\Vdash\CompSec_s(r)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
M,p\Vdash\Sec_s(r).
\]
In particular, strong contextuality is absence of a compatible family at the
set-valued level; it is not the matching-without-amalgamation case
\(\CompSec_s(r)\land\neg\Sec_s(r)\) of this paper.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The event presheaf
\(\mathcal E(U)=\prod_{x\in U}O_x\) is a sheaf. Hence a compatible family
\((s_C)\) glues uniquely to a global assignment \(s\), and its restrictions
remain in the prescribed supports. Conversely, restriction of such an
assignment gives a compatible supported family. This proves the first three
identifications. The fourth is the defining limit formula for
\(\widehat S_e(X)\); the plus construction for the cover
\(\mathcal M\to X\) gives the same set in the sheafification. The displayed
equivalence follows immediately.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Support versus probabilistic contextuality]\label{rem:support-vs-probabilistic-contextuality}
The proposition concerns the possibilistic support of \(e\). Probabilistic
noncontextuality asks instead for a distribution on
\(\prod_{x\in X}O_x\) whose marginals are the given distributions \(e_C\).
That is a fibre-extension problem for the distribution presheaf, and is not
determined by \(S_e\): empirical models with the same support can have
different probabilistic noncontextuality behaviour.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical split stack and the degree obstruction]\label{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface}
Let \(e\) be a finite empirical model on the context site above.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item There is a canonical banded stack lift with zero band,
\[
\mathfrak E_e^0:=\operatorname{Disc}(aS_e),
\qquad
\pi_0(\mathfrak E_e^0)\cong aS_e.
\]
Here \(\operatorname{Disc}\) regards a sheaf of sets as a stack of discrete
groupoids.
\item More generally, after an abelian sheaf \(\Band\) has been supplied,
there is a canonical split \(\Band\)-banded extension
\[
\mathfrak E_e^{\mathrm{spl}}:=
\operatorname{Disc}(aS_e)\times\mathsf B\Band.
\]
Every component gerbe of this extension is neutral, and therefore every
Giraud class supplied by
\Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} is zero.
\item The assignments in \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} are pseudonatural
under context refinements: there are coherent banded equivalences
\[
u_\rho^{-1}\mathfrak E_e^0\simeq
\mathfrak E_{\rho^*e}^0,
\qquad
u_\rho^{-1}\mathfrak E_e^{\mathrm{spl}}\simeq
\mathfrak E_{\rho^*e}^{\mathrm{spl}}
\]
in the second formula whenever the supplied bands are identified under
pullback.
\item The AB and AMB constructions do not produce the non-split degree-two
data required by this paper. More precisely, fix
\(C_0\in\mathcal M\) and \(s\in S_e(C_0)\).
Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa form the free-abelian presheaf
\(\mathcal F_e=\mathbb Z[S_e]\), its relative kernel
\(\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0}\), and a class
\[
\gamma_e(s)\in
\check H^1(\mathcal M,\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0}).
\]
This is relative \v{C}ech cohomology of a presheaf, and the class is the
isomorphism class of an
\(\mathcal F_{e,\overline C_0}\)-torsor trivialized by
\(\mathcal M\). It is not a derived \(H^2\) Giraud class for a sheaf band
\cite{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,Caru2017}.
\item There is no comparison which recovers these AMB classes, for all finite
empirical models, from the component-section obstruction map of any banded stack lift
whose component sheaf is \(aS_e\). Indeed, if \(e\) is strongly contextual,
then
\[
(aS_e)(X)=\varnothing,
\]
so the component-section obstruction map
\[
\delta_{\mathfrak E_e}:(aS_e)(X)\longrightarrow
H^2(\mathcal D_{\mathcal M},\Band)
\]
has empty domain, whereas AMB classes are defined for the local sections
\(s\in S_e(C_0)\) and can be nonzero, as in their GHZ and
Kochen--Specker examples.
\end{enumerate}
In \textup{(i)}, \emph{canonical} means that the construction is the
composite of the universal sheafification functor and the discrete-stack
functor, with no choices, and that the displayed refinement equivalences
satisfy the usual pseudofunctor coherence. It does not mean that all
banded stack lifts of \(S_e\) are equivalent.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The discrete groupoid construction preserves descent, so
\(\operatorname{Disc}(aS_e)\) is a stack and its connected-component sheaf is
exactly \(aS_e\). Its automorphism sheaves are zero, proving \textup{(i)}.
The classifying stack \(\mathsf B\Band\) has one local component and
automorphism sheaf \(\Band\). Taking its product with the discrete stack
therefore proves the band and component assertions in \textup{(ii)}. The
global object represented by the identity \(\Band\)-torsor neutralizes each
component gerbe, so its Giraud class vanishes.

Inverse image for the morphism of context sites commutes, up to its canonical
isomorphism, with associated sheaves, discrete stacks, products, and
classifying stacks. Together with
\(S_{\rho^*e}\cong u_\rho^*S_e\), this gives the equivalences and their
coherence in \textup{(iii)}.

The construction of \(\gamma_e(s)\) and its degree are those of
\cite[Sec.~4]{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012}. The torsor
classification is \cite[Prop.~6.3]{Caru2017}, proving \textup{(iv)}. Finally,
\Cref{prop:ab-compatibility-translation} identifies strong contextuality with
emptiness of \((aS_e)(X)\). The component-section obstruction map of
\Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} is indexed by precisely
that set, while \(\gamma_e(s)\) is indexed by a local section. This proves
the asserted failure in \textup{(v)}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact limit of transfer to empirical models]\label{thm:unique-branch-contextuality-comparison}
For finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical models, the set-valued
local-to-global statements of \Cref{prop:ab-compatibility-translation}
transfer functorially. The later banded and homological theorems transfer
only after a band and a non-split banded stack lift have been
supplied as additional data. In particular:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item the canonical split extension gives only zero Giraud classes and zero
homological image subgroups;
\item the characterization
\[
d(G)\le 2\beta
\quad\text{and}\quad
G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}
\]
remains a construction theorem for the chosen wedge-of-spheres good-cover, band, and
two-component cocycle data of
\Cref{thm:bouquet-two-branch-resolution}; it is not a characterization of
groups canonically attached to empirical models;
\item without an additional degree-shifting construction, the Giraud
\(H^2\)-class neither recovers nor refines the AMB relative
\(\check H^1\)-obstruction.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first and third assertions are
\Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface}(ii),(iv)--(v). The bouquet theorem
starts from a prescribed finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and
chosen componentwise homomorphisms
\(H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A\). None of those data is selected by a bare empirical
model, so its group classification cannot be transported through the split
construction. This proves the second assertion.
\end{proof}

 succeeded in 155ms:
This is the last clause of \Cref{thm:branch-visibility-monotonicity} rewritten on a logarithmic scale.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Readout-preserving rewrites}

\begin{definition}[Readout-preserving rewrite]\label{def:value-preserving-rewrite}
A \emph{readout expression} is any term whose semantic role at a state is determined by a typed readout. A rewrite
\[
E\leadsto E'
\]
between readout expressions is \emph{value preserving} if for every state $p$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $\Read_p(E)$ is defined if and only if $\Read_p(E')$ is defined,
\item whenever defined, $\Read_p(E)=\Read_p(E')$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Readout-preserving rewrites do not create facts]\label{prop:value-preserving-no-creation}
If $E\leadsto E'$ is value preserving and
\[
\Read_p(E')=v
\qquad\text{with}\qquad
v\neq \Indet,
\]
then
\[
\Read_p(E)=v.
\]
In particular, a readout-preserving rewrite cannot turn an undefined or null expression into a genuinely new value claim.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{def:value-preserving-rewrite}, definedness is preserved in both directions, and whenever the readouts are defined they agree. Hence the non-null readout of $E'$ forces the same non-null readout for $E$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalization does not create facts]\label{cor:normalization-no-fact-creation}
Let
\[
E=E_0\leadsto E_1\leadsto\cdots\leadsto E_n=E'
\]
be a finite sequence of readout-preserving rewrites. If $\Read_p(E')=v\neq \Indet$, then $\Read_p(E)=v$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply \Cref{prop:value-preserving-no-creation} inductively along the rewrite sequence.
\end{proof}

\section{A split GHZ/Mermin amplitude-lift template}\label{sec:appendix-ghz}

The GHZ/Mermin model provides a convenient illustration of the split lift in
\Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface}. The role of this section is
correspondingly limited: it records chosen representatives for that split
lift, not a constructed non-split finite-nerve GHZ example. In particular, it
does not supply a canonical finite nerve, a normalized $2$-cocycle, a
\v{C}ech-to-derived comparison map, or a nonzero value of $K_\omega$ for GHZ.

Let $e_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ be the Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model obtained from the GHZ state \cite{GreenbergerHorneZeilinger1989,Mermin1990,AbramskyBrandenburger2011}, situated in the Kochen--Specker tradition \cite{KochenSpecker1967}. Related topological and cohomological treatments of contextuality include \cite{OkayRaussendorf2016,OkayRobertsBartlettRaussendorf2017,OkayTyhurstRaussendorf2018,Aasnaess2022}. The measurement cover consists of the four contexts
\[
C_{XXX},\ C_{XYY},\ C_{YXY},\ C_{YYX},
\]
where, for instance, $C_{XYY}$ records the joint measurement in which the first observer measures $X$ and the other two measure $Y$. Each context carries outcomes in $\{\pm 1\}^3$, and the GHZ support presheaf $S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ selects exactly the assignments whose parity matches the GHZ constraints: $+1$ on $XXX$ and $-1$ on the three $XYY$-type contexts.

\begin{definition}[Banded groupoid lift of a support presheaf]\label{def:amplitude-lift}
Let $S_e$ be the support presheaf of a finite empirical model on a measurement-cover site $\mathcal C_a$. An \emph{banded groupoid lift of the support presheaf} of $S_e$ with band $\Band$ is a banded groupoid lift
\[
\mathfrak P_e\to \mathcal C_a
\]
together with an identification
\[
\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_e)\cong S_e.
\]
Equivalently, an banded groupoid lift of the support presheaf is a choice of local lift object objects and phase-sensitive transition isomorphisms whose isomorphism classes recover the supported local assignments.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Support data versus non-split amplitude data]\label{rem:amplitude-lift-choice}
The support presheaf canonically determines the split lift of
\Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface}, but that lift has only neutral
component gerbes. It does not determine a non-split banded groupoid lift of the support presheaf, a
nonzero derived branch class, or a nonzero value of $K_\omega$. Such claims
for empirical support presheaves are therefore relative to additional lift
data.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Chosen GHZ phase-line lift]\label{lem:ghz-prestack}
Let $a=[r]_p$ be the GHZ base object and $\mathcal C_a:=\mathcal C_{p,s}/a$. Fix, for each object $U$ of $\mathcal C_a$ and each supported local assignment $s\in S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}(U)$, a one-dimensional complex line $L_{U,s}$ generated by a chosen local GHZ amplitude, together with restriction isomorphisms compatible with restriction of assignments. Let $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}}(U)$ be the groupoid whose objects are the pairs
\[
(s,L_{U,s}),
\qquad
s\in S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}(U),
\]
and whose automorphisms are the signs $\{\pm 1\}\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ acting on the chosen line. Then $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}}\to\mathcal C_a$ is an banded groupoid lift of the support presheaf of $S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ with band $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. Its stackification is bandedly equivalent to
\[
\operatorname{Disc}(aS_{\mathrm{GHZ}})
\times\mathsf B(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z),
\]
so every component gerbe is neutral.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By construction, restriction along $V\to U$ sends $(s,L_{U,s})$ to the restricted supported assignment together with the chosen restricted line, so the fibres form a category fibred in groupoids over $\mathcal C_a$. The automorphism sheaf of every object is the constant sheaf $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, acting by sign changes on the one-dimensional line. Forgetting the line remembers only the supported assignment, and two objects are isomorphic exactly when they have the same supported assignment. Hence
\[
\pi_0^{\mathrm{pre}}(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}})\cong S_{\mathrm{GHZ}},
\]
so \Cref{def:amplitude-lift} is satisfied.
The compatible choice of one line for every supported assignment gives an
equivalence with the split prestack having those assignments as components
and $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ as each automorphism sheaf. Stackification
therefore gives the displayed split stack, whose identity torsor supplies a
global object in each component.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Limit of the chosen GHZ/Mermin lift]\label{thm:ghz-realization}
Let $S_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ be the GHZ support presheaf, and fix the chosen banded groupoid lift of the support presheaf $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}}$ of \Cref{lem:ghz-prestack}. Suppose, in addition, that one has chosen a stackification
\[
\mathfrak L_{\mathrm{GHZ}}:=a(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}})
\]
and a cofinal family of covers
\[
\Cov_{\mathrm{GHZ}}^{\mathrm{acyc}}(a)
\]
such that the terminal-fibre essential-surjectivity and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison clauses of \Cref{def:gluing-sensitive-realization} hold for this chosen lift. Then
\[
(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{GHZ}},\mathfrak L_{\mathrm{GHZ}},\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z,\Cov_{\mathrm{GHZ}}^{\mathrm{acyc}})
\]
is a gluing-sensitive banded lift datum for the chosen split GHZ amplitude
lift, but every Giraud class furnished by its component gerbes is zero. In
particular, it does not recover the nonzero relative degree-one classes of
\cite{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012}, and it yields no nonzero value of
$K_\omega$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\Cref{lem:ghz-prestack} identifies the stackification as a split extension.
The additional assumptions are exactly the remaining clauses in
\Cref{def:gluing-sensitive-realization}. The general theorems therefore
apply, but neutrality of every component gerbe forces all resulting Giraud
classes, homological evaluation maps, and homological image subgroups to vanish.
\end{proof}

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

\begin{definition}[Common refinements and completeness]\label{def:fusion-state}
Let $K\subseteq J$ be finite, and suppose that for each $j\in K$ there is a single-axis refinement $p\rightsquigarrow_j q_j$. A state $u$ is a \emph{common refinement} for the family $(q_j)_{j\in K}$ if
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_K u
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
u\le q_j\ \text{for every }j\in K.
\]
The indexed refinement system \emph{admits all required common refinements} if every finite pairwise commuting family of single-axis refinements admits a common refinement.
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Explicit lifting principle]\label{cor:explicit-lifting}
Assume that all required common refinements exist. Let $K\subseteq J$ be finite, and for each $j\in K$ let
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_j q_j
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\Read_{q_j,s_j}(r_j)=v_j\neq \Indet.
\]
If the single-axis refinements are pairwise commuting at $p$, then there exists a common refinement $u$ such that
\[
\Read_{u,s_j}(r_j)=v_j
\qquad
(\forall j\in K).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By the common-refinement hypothesis there exists a common refinement $u$ with $u\le q_j$ for all $j\in K$. Since each $q_j$ carries a determined typed readout, \Cref{prop:typed-readout-persistence} transports that readout to the common refinement $u$. Thus all axis-wise readout judgments hold simultaneously at one state.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Componentwise obstruction monotonicity}

The obstruction theory of \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} becomes dynamic once global component sections and their component gerbes are transported along refinement. In the model classes just described, the basic structural fact is that refinement can only shrink the homological image subgroup and enlarge its cokernel.

\begin{proposition}[Refinement monotonicity of componentwise homological cokernels]\label{thm:branch-visibility-monotonicity}
Let $q\le p$, let $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ be admitted at both states, and write
\[
a_p=[r]_p,
\qquad
a_q=[r]_q.
\]
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item there is a morphism of slice sites
\[
f_{q,p}:\mathcal C_{q,s}/a_q\to \mathcal C_{p,s}/a_p;
\]
\item the banded groupoid lift at $q$ is equivalent to the pullback of the banded groupoid lift at $p$ along $f_{q,p}$;
\item global component sections pull back along refinement, and for a component section $w\in \Vis_{q,s}(r)$ lying above $v\in \Vis_{p,s}(r)$ the corresponding component gerbes satisfy
\[
\mathfrak G_w\simeq f_{q,p}^*(\mathfrak G_v);
\]
\item compatible finite nerve representatives have been chosen together with a simplicial refinement map
\[
N(f_{q,p}):N(\mathcal U_q)\to N(\mathcal U_p)
\]
such that the induced component obstruction classes satisfy
\[
\omega_w=N(f_{q,p})^*(\omega_v)
\]
with the same finite abelian band $A$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
X_v\subseteq X_w,
\qquad
K_w\subseteq K_v,
\qquad
Q_w\twoheadrightarrow Q_v,
\qquad
|K_w|\le |K_v|.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The pullback of gerbes is again a gerbe, and the induced cohomology class is the pullback of the original one \cite[Tag 06NY]{StacksProject}, \cite[Theorem~3.11]{BerghSchnurer2021}. Naturality of the universal coefficient map with respect to the simplicial refinement map $N(f_{q,p})$ gives the cohomological compatibility needed below. Let $\chi\in X_v$. Then
\[
\chi_*(\omega_v)=0.
\]
Applying the pullback $N(f_{q,p})^*$ gives
\[
\chi_*(\omega_w)=\chi_*\bigl(N(f_{q,p})^*(\omega_v)\bigr)=N(f_{q,p})^*\bigl(\chi_*(\omega_v)\bigr)=0,
\]
so $\chi\in X_w$. Hence $X_v\subseteq X_w$.

By \Cref{thm:intrinsic-visible-quotient},
\[
K_v=\bigcap_{\chi\in X_v}\ker\chi
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
K_w=\bigcap_{\chi\in X_w}\ker\chi.
\]
Since $X_v\subseteq X_w$, intersecting over the larger family gives the smaller subgroup, so $K_w\subseteq K_v$. Therefore the quotient map $A\twoheadrightarrow A/K_v$ factors through $A/K_w$, yielding a surjection
\[
Q_w=A/K_w\twoheadrightarrow A/K_v=Q_v.
\]
For finite groups, $K_w\subseteq K_v$ implies $|K_w|\le |K_v|$.
\end{proof}

\begin{example}[A strict drop under refinement]\label{ex:refinement-drop}
Let $A=\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, and let $r$ be admitted at $q\le p$.
Assume that at $p$ there is one global component section $v$ and a component obstruction class
\[
\omega_v\in H^2(N(\mathcal U_p),A)
\]
with
\[
K_v=\langle 2\rangle\subseteq A.
\]
Hence
\[
Q_v=A/K_v\cong \mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z.
\]

Suppose $r$ has a unique component section $w$ above $v$ at the refinement $q$, and the induced pullback class
\[
\omega_w=f_{q,p}^*(\omega_v)
\]
is trivial in $H^2(N(\mathcal U_q),A)$. Then
\[
K_w=\{0\},\qquad Q_w=A/K_w\cong A.
\]
By \Cref{thm:branch-visibility-monotonicity}, the map
\[
Q_w\longrightarrow Q_v
\]
is the quotient mod~$2$, so $|K_w|<|K_v|$ and the logarithmic fibre cardinality decreases strictly under this refinement.
\end{example}

\begin{corollary}[Refinement decreases presentation-relative logarithmic fibre cardinality]\label{cor:branch-budget-monotonicity}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:branch-visibility-monotonicity}, refinement can only enlarge the quotient and can never increase the presentation-relative minimum auxiliary register size of the componentwise quotient map:
\[
\log_2|K_w|\le \log_2|K_v|.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}

\appendix

We collect two auxiliary topics. The first concerns the refinement-dynamic extension together with finite-state complexity bounds for the associated information-determination notions. The second gives the GHZ/Mermin banded groupoid lift of the support presheaf mentioned in the introduction.
\section{Finite-state complexity bounds}\label{sec:appendix-complexity}

We record the finite-state upper bounds for the information-determination notions attached to the refinement-dynamic extension of the semantics.

For this appendix, assume that the indexed refinement system is finite and that a distinguished formula $\chi$ is part of the input together with polynomial-time decidable tables for the relations
\[
q\mapsto (M,q\Vdash\chi),
\qquad
q\mapsto (M,q\Vdash\neg\chi),
\qquad
q\mapsto (\mathrm{info}_j(q))_{j\in J}.
\]
The finite information maps for refinement axes $\mathrm{info}_j$ of \Cref{def:axis-information-maps} are assumed to be part of the input model; agreement of $K$-information between two states is checked by comparing $\mathrm{info}_j(q)=\mathrm{info}_j(r)$ for each $j\in K$. This is the natural finite encoding once the underlying semantic state graph has already been computed and the information-determination problems are asked over that graph. No matching lower bounds are claimed here.

We consider the decision problems \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, and \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} associated with \Cref{def:axis-support,def:axis-indispensability}. For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} we use the standard class $\mathrm{D}^P$ in the sense of Papadimitriou and Yannakakis \cite{PapadimitriouYannakakis1984}.

\begin{proposition}[Complexity upper bounds]\label{thm:axis-complexity-upper-bounds}
Under the finite encoding above, the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item \textup{\textsc{Determining}} belongs to coNP.
\item \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} belongs to NP.
\item \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} belongs to $\mathrm{D}^P$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For \textup{\textsc{Determining}}, failure of determination is witnessed by a pair $(q,r)$ of $K$-reachable states that agree on the relevant $K$-information, both decide $\chi$, and satisfy opposite truth values. Reachability, agreement of axis information, and decision of $\chi$ are all polynomial-time checkable in the finite input, so the complement of \textup{\textsc{Determining}} is in NP.

For \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}}, a witness is again a pair $(q,r)$, now only required to agree on all axes except the distinguished axis $j$ and to satisfy opposite truth values of $\chi$. This certificate is polynomially checkable, so \textup{\textsc{NecessaryAxis}} lies in NP.

For \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}}, the condition that $K$ determines $\chi$ is in coNP by the first clause. The condition that every axis in $K$ is necessary is in NP, because one may guess one witness pair for each axis $j\in K$, and the total certificate size remains polynomial. By \Cref{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}, the conjunction of these two conditions characterizes minimal information-determining axis sets, so \textup{\textsc{MinDetermining}} lies in $\mathrm{D}^P$.
\end{proof}

\section{Refinement dynamics}\label{sec:appendix-dynamics}

This section contains the formal refinement-dynamic material.

\subsection{Refinement dynamics and information determination}\label{sec:appendix-multiaxis-refinement}

The previous sections analyzed satisfaction at a fixed state. We now treat refinement itself as a dynamics: the satisfaction clause stays unchanged, but the set of assignments may shrink along different axes of information. The results apply to model classes in which refinement induces morphisms of slice sites and compatible maps of finite nerves.

\subsubsection{Dynamic refinement}

\begin{definition}[Indexed refinement system]\label{def:multi-axis-dynamic-structure}
Fix a model $M$. A \emph{indexed refinement system} on $M$ is a tuple
\[
\mathfrak{D}=\bigl(\St(M),\le,\tau,J,\{\rightsquigarrow_j\}_{j\in J}\bigr),
\]
where $J$ is an axis set, each $\rightsquigarrow_j$ is a single-axis refinement relation satisfying
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_j q \Longrightarrow q\le p,
\]
and $\tau:\St(M)\to T$ maps states to a linearly ordered set $T$ such that
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_j q \Longrightarrow \tau(q)\ge \tau(p).
\]
For finite $K\subseteq J$, write $p\rightsquigarrow_K q$ if $q$ is reachable from $p$ by a finite chain of refinements using only axes in $K$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Updates preserve satisfaction]\label{prop:updates-preserve-forcing}
If $p\rightsquigarrow_K q$ and $M,p\Vdash\varphi$, then $M,q\Vdash\varphi^\uparrow$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Every indexed step is a refinement by \Cref{def:multi-axis-dynamic-structure}, so $q\le p$. The claim is therefore immediate from \Cref{prop:forcing-persistence}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Delayed decidability]\label{def:delayed-decidability}
Let $p\rightsquigarrow_K q$. We say that $\varphi$ undergoes \emph{delayed decidability} from $p$ to $q$ if
\[
M,p\nVdash\varphi,\qquad
M,p\nVdash\neg\varphi,\qquad
\text{but}\qquad
M,q\Downarrow\varphi.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Delayed decidability does not create truth]\label{prop:delayed-no-new-truth}
If $\varphi$ undergoes delayed decidability in a transition $p\rightsquigarrow_K q$, then the passage from $p$ to $q$ acts by eliminating assignments from $R_p$ rather than by changing the truth conditions of $\varphi$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
If $M,p\Vdash\varphi$ or $M,p\Vdash\neg\varphi$ already held, then \Cref{prop:updates-preserve-forcing} would preserve that judgment at $q$. Hence delayed decidability can occur only because the refinement $q\le p$ has discarded assignments that formerly gave incompatible outcomes. The semantic clause for $\varphi$ itself has not changed.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Delayed classification is non-retrocausal]\label{prop:nonretrocausal-delayed-classification}
Let $p\rightsquigarrow_K q$, and suppose that $q$ is $\tau$-minimal among the $K$-reachable states that decide $\varphi$. Then every $u$ with
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_K u
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\tau(u)<\tau(q)
\]
is still undecided on $\varphi$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
If some earlier $u$ with $\tau(u)<\tau(q)$ already decided $\varphi$, then $q$ would not be $\tau$-minimal among the deciding states reachable from $p$. Thus no earlier stage carries the later decision. The decision at $q$ records newly available discriminatory power at $q$, not a change in the past.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Axis support and explicit lifting}

\begin{definition}[Finite information maps for refinement axes]\label{def:axis-information-maps}
Fix a indexed refinement system $\mathfrak{D}$ on a model $M$. For each axis $j\in J$, assume there is a finite set $I_j$ and a map
\[
\mathrm{info}_j:\{q\in\St(M)\mid p\rightsquigarrow_K q\text{ for some finite }K\ni j\}\longrightarrow I_j.
\]
For states $q$ and $r$ reachable from $p$ via $K$-refinements and a subset $L\subseteq K$, we say that $q$ and $r$ \emph{agree on $L$-information} if
\[
\mathrm{info}_j(q)=\mathrm{info}_j(r)
\qquad
\text{for every }j\in L.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Information-determining axis sets and minimality]\label{def:axis-support}
Let $K\subseteq J$ be finite. We say that $K$ \emph{determines} a formula $\varphi$ at $p$, written $K\triangleright_p\varphi$, if whenever
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_K q,\qquad
p\rightsquigarrow_K r,
\]
and both $q$ and $r$ decide $\varphi$, agreement of the $K$-information (in the sense of \Cref{def:axis-information-maps}) implies agreement of the decision. An information-determining set $K$ is \emph{minimal} if no proper subset of $K$ still determines $\varphi$ at $p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Necessity of a refinement axis]\label{def:axis-indispensability}
Let $K\subseteq J$ be finite and let $j\in K$. We say that $j$ is \emph{necessary relative to $K$} for $\varphi$ at $p$ if there exist states $q$ and $r$ with
\[
p\rightsquigarrow_K q,\qquad
p\rightsquigarrow_K r,
\]
such that $q$ and $r$ agree on $(K\setminus\{j\})$-information (in the sense of \Cref{def:axis-information-maps}), while
\[
M,q\Vdash\varphi
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
M,r\Vdash\neg\varphi.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Necessity of a refinement axis implies minimality]\label{prop:indispensability-implies-minimality}
If $K\triangleright_p\varphi$ and every $j\in K$ is necessary relative to $K$ for $\varphi$ at $p$, then $K$ is a minimal information-determining axis set for $\varphi$ at $p$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Assume that a proper subset $L\subsetneq K$ still determined $\varphi$, and choose $j\in K\setminus L$. Any two states that agree on all axes in $K\setminus\{j\}$ automatically agree on all axes in $L$, contradicting the necessity of the refinement axis $j$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Pairwise commuting refinements]\label{def:axis-orthogonality}
Two axes $j,k\in J$ are \emph{pairwise commuting at $p$} if whenever

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct.  \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and
+$K_1+K_2=G$ if and only if
+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
+arbitrary empirical model.

+We now describe the framework.  An information state
+$p=(\Gamma_p,R_p)$ is a nonempty team $R_p$ of assignments with common finite

+\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum

K_\lambda=\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda)
\qquad
(\lambda\in\Lambda).
\qedhere
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact subgroup classification on torsion-free second homology]\label{cor:torsion-free-h2-classification}
Assume the full hypothesis package of \Cref{thm:mixed-branch-realization}: a
fixed finite nerve $N=N(\mathcal U)$ in a formal \v{C}ech good-cover site,
a trivialized constant finite abelian band $A$, the Leray comparison
isomorphism for the finite-nerve classes, the constructed realization
prestack, and essential surjectivity on the terminal fibre. Assume
in addition that
\[
H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z^\beta
\]
for some integer $\beta\ge 0$. Let $(K_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ be a family of subgroups of $A$. Then the following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item There exist a state $p$, an admissible parameter $r:\mathsf{Ref}_s$ on the fixed nerve $N$, and a bijection
\[
\Vis_{p,s}(r)\cong \Lambda
\]
such that the branch indexed by $\lambda$ has presentation-relative homological image subgroup
\[
K_\lambda.
\]
\item Every subgroup $K_\lambda$ is generated by at most $\beta$ elements.
\end{enumerate}
When these conditions hold,
\[
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{br}}(r)\cong A\Big/\bigcap_{\lambda\in\Lambda}K_\lambda,
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{unif}}(r)\cong A\Big/\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}K_\lambda,
\]
and
\[
M,p\Vdash \Sec_s(r)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
K_\lambda=0\ \text{for some}\ \lambda\in\Lambda.
\]
In particular, a single branch realizes surjective homological evaluation
\[
K_\omega=A
\]
if and only if $A$ is generated by at most $\beta$ elements. For $\beta=1$, the realizable single-component presentation-relative homological image subgroups are exactly the cyclic subgroups of $A$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Assume \textup{(i)}. For any branch on the fixed finite nerve satisfying the
finite-nerve comparison hypotheses, its presentation-relative homological image subgroup is by
definition the image of the homological evaluation map attached to its branch
obstruction class. Since
\[
H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0,
\]
the universal coefficient comparison identifies that evaluation map with a
homomorphism from $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)$ to $A$. Thus, for each $\lambda$, there
exists a homomorphism
\[
\phi_\lambda:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A
\]
with
\[
K_\lambda=\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda).
\]
After choosing an identification
\[
H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z^\beta,
\]
the image of $\phi_\lambda$ is generated by the images of the $\beta$ standard basis vectors. Hence $K_\lambda$ is generated by at most $\beta$ elements. Therefore \textup{(ii)} holds.

Assume conversely that \textup{(ii)} holds. For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, choose generators
\[
k_{\lambda,1},\dots,k_{\lambda,\beta}\in K_\lambda
\]
of $K_\lambda$, allowing repetitions and zeros when fewer than $\beta$ generators are needed. Define
\[
\phi_\lambda:\mathbb Z^\beta\to A,
\qquad
(n_1,\dots,n_\beta)\longmapsto \sum_{j=1}^{\beta} n_j k_{\lambda,j}.
\]
Then
\[
\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda)=K_\lambda.
\]
Transporting these maps across the chosen isomorphism
\[
H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb Z^\beta
\]
and applying \Cref{thm:mixed-branch-realization} yields the required state $p$, reference $r$, and branch family. Hence \textup{(i)} holds.

The quotient formulas are those of \Cref{thm:mixed-branch-realization}(v). The global-section criterion follows from \Cref{thm:mixed-branch-realization}(iii), because
\[
K_\lambda=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{Im}(\phi_\lambda)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\phi_\lambda=0.
\]
For the maximal-collapse claim, take $\Lambda$ to be a singleton and $K_\omega=A$. Then the equivalence between \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} says exactly that such a branch exists if and only if $A$ is generated by at most $\beta$ elements. The final sentence is the case $\beta=1$.
\end{proof}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements. +\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. The contribution of the paper is accordingly structural: the extension chain separates the semantic layers, the empirical-model comparison proves exactly where an extra categorical degree enters, and the obstruction class gives rise to a groupoid-indexed invariant only after branchwise lift data and a finite nerve presentation have been fixed.
+The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results. The appendix collects the supplementary material on refinement dynamics and the GHZ/Mermin example.
+\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt,labelindent=0pt]
+\item[Information state $p=(\Gamma,R)$.]
+A nonempty team $R$ of assignments with common finite context $\Gamma$.
+\item[Universal team satisfaction.]
+$M,p\Vdash\varphi$ means that every assignment in the team of $p$ satisfies
+$\varphi$ in ordinary Tarskian semantics.
+\item[Singleton-state embedding.]
+The map from an assignment to its singleton team, preserving ordinary
+satisfaction.
+\item[Truth-preserving reduct expansion.]
+An expansion whose higher models preserve lower-language satisfaction after
+the specified model reduct and state projection; consequence conservativity
+is not part of the definition.
+\item[Typed expansion class.]
+The class of all supplied higher-layer data of the stipulated types over a
+fixed lower model.
+\item[Admissible parameter $r$.]
+An element satisfying the primitive predicate $\Adm_s$; the predicate records
+exactly that the site and presheaf data stipulated in the relevant typed model
+are attached to $r$.
+\item[Base object $a=[r]_p$.]
+The object of the reference-refinement site associated to the pair $(p,r)$;
+the brackets do not denote an equivalence class.
+\item[Reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$.]
+The thin category of base objects ordered by refinement, equipped with the
+specified pretopology and pullbacks.
+\item[Presheaf of local sections $F_{p,s}$.]
+The functor $\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.
+\item[Matching without amalgamation at $a$.]
+A matching family exists on a cover of $a$, but $F_{p,s}(a)$ is empty.
+\item[Gluing-sensitive banded lift datum.]
+A banded groupoid lift, its stackification and component-sheaf identification,
+terminal-fibre essential surjectivity, and a \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison
+hypothesis.
+\item[Pullback-stable representative choice.]
+A choice of one representative of each presheaf section that is preserved
+strictly by every pullback; ``representative-rigid'' abbreviates this condition.
+\item[Global component section $v$.]
+An element of $\pi_0(\mathfrak L_r)(a)$, identified with a section of
+$(aF)(a)$.
+\item[Component gerbe $\mathfrak G_v$ and component obstruction $\omega_v$.]
+The full banded substack over $v$ and its Giraud class
+$[\mathfrak G_v]\in H^2(\mathcal C/a,\Band)$.
+\item[Presentation-comparison groupoid.]
+The groupoid freely generated by the specified refinements, cocycle
+replacements, band retrivializations, and their formal inverses; distinct
+zigzags need not give the same comparison.
+\item[Coordinate-image subgroup and cocycle-coordinate quotient.]
+For a chosen cocycle $\alpha$, the subgroup generated by its coordinate values
+and the corresponding quotient $A/H_\alpha$.
+\item[Homological image $K_\omega$ and homological cokernel $Q_\omega$.]
+$\operatorname{Im}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)$ and
+$\operatorname{coker}(\operatorname{ev}_\omega)=A/K_\omega$.
+\item[Label-aware quotient.]
+$A/(\bigcap_vK_v)$, equivalently the image of $A$ in the product of the
+componentwise homological cokernels.
+\item[Common-character quotient.]
+$A/(\sum_vK_v)$, detected by the characters that annihilate every $K_v$.
+\item[Component-forgetting kernel.]
+The kernel of the canonical map from the label-aware quotient to the
+common-character quotient, namely $(\sum_vK_v)/(\bigcap_vK_v)$.
+\item[Fibre-separating auxiliary register.]
+A finite set used in an injective lift of a quotient map; its minimum
+cardinality is the largest quotient-fibre cardinality.
+\item[Finite intersection site associated to a cover nerve.]
+The finite thin pullback site generated by the formal intersections indexed by
+the nerve, with an initial object representing empty intersections.
+\end{description}

 \begin{abstract}
-We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For admitted references, compatible local sectionability is equivalent, on slice-separated reference slices, to nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor. A lower-fragment separation theorem shows that compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct. At the groupoid-valued level, representative rigidity and global conservativity force surjectivity of the sheafification unit at the terminal fibre. For banded realization-stack extensions, each visible branch determines a Giraud class in $H^2$. Every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical refinement-functorial split extension, but all its Giraud classes vanish; the Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa obstruction is instead a relative $H^1$ torsor class indexed by a local section. Thus the banded theory requires extra lift data. For finite abelian bands its homological evaluation map controls a presentation-object visible quotient. On bouquet good covers, a nonzero finite abelian group occurs as a pure two-branch resolution kernel exactly when $d(G)\le 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group, but this classification does not canonically transfer to empirical models.
+A nonzero finite abelian group $G$ occurs as a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary nonzero image subgroups on the chosen good-cover site of a wedge of $\beta$ copies of $S^2$ if and only if $d(G)\leq 2\beta$ and $G$ is not a cyclic $p$-group.  This follows from the universal coefficient theorem after fixing a finite nerve, a constant finite abelian band, and a banded groupoid lift of a presheaf.  For a component-gerbe class $\omega$, evaluation on $H_2$ gives $\operatorname{ev}_\omega:H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\to A$; its image and cokernel determine the componentwise and aggregate quotients.  When $H_1(N,\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_2(N,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^\beta$, the possible image subgroups are exactly those generated by at most $\beta$ elements.  Under explicit separatedness, representability, and \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison hypotheses, matching families without global amalgamations correspond to non-neutral component gerbes.  This derived $H^2$ invariant is not the relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ obstruction of Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa; only the underlying support-presheaf comparison is functorial.
 \end{abstract}

 \section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
 
-Sheaf-theoretic semantics offers a natural language for the passage from local data to global objects. In logical applications, and in particular in sheaf-theoretic analyses of contextuality \cite{AbramskyBrandenburger2011,AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,AbramskyBarbosaKishidaLalMansfield2015,Caru2017,Caru2018,Montanhano2021}, the central question is whether compatible local families glue to global sections. The classical tools for measuring the failure of gluing are gerbes, obstruction classes, and cohomological invariants \cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}. In this paper we study that question in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations, with the aim of separating the successive layers at which genuinely new local-to-global structure appears.
+Fix an integer $\beta\geq 1$.  Our main classification theorem concerns the
+good-cover intersection site obtained from barycentric open-star covers of a
+finite model of the wedge $\bigvee_{j=1}^{\beta}S^2$.  A nonzero finite
+abelian group $G$ occurs as the kernel of the canonical map
+\[
+ A/\bigl(K_1\cap K_2\bigr)\longrightarrow A/\bigl(K_1+K_2\bigr)
+\]
+for two non-neutral component gerbes with $K_1\cap K_2=0$ and
+$K_1+K_2=G$ if and only if
+\[
+ d(G)\leq 2\beta
+ \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+ G\text{ is not a cyclic }p\text{-group}.
+\]
+Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$.  In the terminology
+fixed below, this kernel is the \emph{component-forgetting kernel}; the
+displayed special case is a two-component label-loss kernel with complementary
+nonzero image subgroups.  The statement is an existence and classification
+result for the chosen site, band, and lift data, not an invariant of an
+arbitrary empirical model.
 
-Our starting point is the extension chain
+The standard input is as follows.  We use universal satisfaction on nonempty
+teams of assignments, presheaves and their sheafifications, stackification of
+categories fibred in groupoids, the classification of banded gerbes by
+Giraud's $H^2$, the \v{C}ech-to-derived comparison on the specified Leray
+covers, the universal coefficient theorem, and elementary structure theory
+and duality for finite abelian groups
+\cite{Giraud1971,Breen2006,Hatcher2002}.  Our contributions are the organization

The map $\mathbb{L}_0\hookrightarrow\mathbb{L}_1$ is a singleton semantic embedding, whereas the later steps are conservative extensions in the sense of \Cref{def:conservative-extension}. Thus the geometric and homological material introduced later does not alter the forcing behaviour of formulas already present in the lower layers.

-The first part of the paper concerns the passage from information states to local objects. \Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification} shows that compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the associated sheafification, and \Cref{thm:sheafification-characterization} proves the converse on slice-separated reference slices. We then prove in \Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility} that the predicates $\CompSec_s$, $\Sec_s$, and $\Null^{\mathrm{glue}}_s$ are not definable by automorphism-invariant, constant-free formulas of the $\mathbb{L}_1$-reduct with one free reference variable. This is only a lower-bound statement for the comparison fragment under consideration, but it isolates a genuine change of behaviour between $\mathbb L_1$ and $\mathbb L_2$.
+We now describe the framework.  An information state
+$p=(\Gamma_p,R_p)$ is a nonempty team $R_p$ of assignments with common finite
+context $\Gamma_p$.  We write $M,p\Vdash\varphi$ when every assignment in
+$R_p$ satisfies $\varphi$ in the ordinary Tarskian sense.  Thus $\Vdash$ is
+universal team satisfaction, not set-theoretic, Kripke, Beth, or
+Kripke--Joyal forcing.  Refinement enlarges the context and may restrict the
+team, which immediately gives persistence.  Point assignments enter through
+the singleton-state embedding.  The later semantic frameworks add typed data
+while preserving the truth of formulas in the reduct; we call these
+truth-preserving reduct expansions, rather than conservative extensions,
+because consequence conservativity is not asserted without an expansion
+theorem for every lower model.
 
-The second part begins once the set-valued local-object functor is enriched by groupoid-valued data. \Cref{thm:canonical-lift-rigidity} gives a rigidity statement for representative-rigid lifts: if the local-object presheaf is slice-separated and a realization prestack admits a strict functorial choice of representatives and is globally conservative at the terminal fibre, then the sheafification unit is surjective there; under $H^1$-vanishing and the same slice-separatedness, this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf at the terminal fibre. Thus gluing-level nullity is necessarily tied to genuinely gluing-sensitive lift data. \Cref{thm:intrinsic-branch-obstruction-extension} identifies the canonicity that survives at this level: once the sheafified local object functor has been lifted to a banded realization stack, the branch obstruction map to derived $H^2$ is intrinsic up to equivalence of banded extensions. For such an extension, visible value classes are the global sections of the sheaf of connected components (\Cref{thm:visible-value-components}), each visible branch determines a banded component gerbe (\Cref{thm:component-gerbe-decomposition}), and, on slice-separated reference slices, \Cref{thm:gerbe-null-semantics} identifies gluing-level absence with the existence of visible branches together with non-neutrality of the corresponding component gerbes.
+For an admissible parameter $r$ at $p$, the paper specifies a thin
+reference-refinement site $\mathcal C_{p,s}$, its base object
+$a=[r]_p$, and a presheaf of local sections
+$F_{p,s}:\mathcal C_{p,s}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$.  A matching family
+without an element of $F_{p,s}(a)$ is the set-valued failure studied here.
+The forward implication from a matching family to a section of the
+sheafification is formal; the converse holds when
+$F_{p,s}|_{\mathcal C_{p,s}/a}$ is separated
+(\Cref{prop:compsec-to-sheafification,thm:sheafification-characterization}).
+The predicates expressing a matching family, a global section, and matching
+without amalgamation are not definable in the automorphism-invariant,
+constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct
+(\Cref{thm:pointwise-irreducibility}).
 
-The empirical-model interface gives a sharp limit to this canonicity.  \Cref{thm:empirical-model-stack-interface} proves that every finite Abramsky--Brandenburger empirical model has a canonical split realization-stack extension, pseudonatural under ordinary refinements of measurement contexts, but every component gerbe in that extension is neutral.  The Abramsky--Mansfield--Barbosa class is a relative \v{C}ech $H^1$ class of a presheaf, equivalently a torsor class \cite{AbramskyMansfieldSoaresBarbosa2012,Caru2017}; it is indexed by a chosen local section.  By contrast, the Giraud map here is a derived $H^2$ class for a sheaf band, indexed by a global component, and for a strongly contextual model that indexing set is empty. +\subsection*{Glossary of retained terminology}
 
-The sheaf-theoretic, gerbe-theoretic, and homological tools used here are classical, and several of the later comparison results are formal once the branchwise intrinsic data have been fixed. +The following short names are used only after their standard-language content
+has been fixed.
 
-The paper is organized as follows. \Cref{sec:preliminaries} fixes the extension chain and the relevant notions of conservativity. \Cref{sec:information-states} recalls forcing over information states. \Cref{sec:null-decomposition} studies local objects, sheafification, and lower-fragment separation. \Cref{sec:gerbe-obstruction} introduces component gerbes and branch obstruction classes. \Cref{sec:homological-visibility} and \Cref{sec:branch-aggregation} contain the homological visibility theory together with the branchwise comparison and realization results.
